Own connected body is skipped; unbreakable/protected blocks and unloaded terrain stop the cut. Charging and Preview never destroy blocks.

dashboard.sablelife.pull_help: Destination = marked face + Start distance; follows the limb. Target release ignores Start distance. Warning sphere stays fixed for this cast. Leave it before activation to dodge. Later entrants are not captured; leaving the sphere or hiding behind a wall (LOS On) releases you. Sideways movement is preserved. No teleport or direct damage. At target uses the nearest eligible target in the search range as the fixed warning/pull center. Stopping distance is the radius around the pull center where attraction brakes/stops, not the target detection range. Defaults: beacon activate warning / beacon ambient pulling. Target-position release needs no Mark. Multiple target Off selects the nearest eligible target; On releases at each eligible target, up to 64. Sphere Blast and Attraction freeze centers at charge/warning start; Area Pulse samples fresh centers per release. No target means no cast. Search range and effect radius are independent; a batch shares one cooldown. Mark mode retains its existing behavior. In Mark mode, Directional funnel uses length and two radii (equal = cylinder). Start distance positions along the original face before horizontal/vertical angles. Target-position release always uses a sphere. Stable suction steers velocity and compensates gravity while pulling, without disabling collision or changing NoGravity. Warning geometry is fixed for the cast; leaving it or losing LOS releases the target.

dashboard.sablelife.redstone_help:
Items in the red/blue slots directly set the external wireless frequency. Leave them empty for Mark only. Marked-face and wireless outputs can run together. Six faces powers the marked block's neighbors. Selected surface supplies the marked block from that face. Reverse signal defaults Off. On swaps zero and the configured strength for both marked and external outputs. Hold: idle high, triggered low. Pulse: idle high, low for the pulse duration, then high again. Disabled, invalid, dormant or master Off always outputs zero. Outputs to this core's Wireless channel; 0 disables it. Enable the channel and select Sequence / internal. Uses strength, Hold/Pulse and inversion. No Mark or frequency items required; all three destinations can work together. Highest strength wins across producers. Use different input/output channels to avoid self-latching. Follow input preserves0â€“15 from Internal wireless, External RX or Anchor power; fixed strength is disabled for these triggers. Always, Move Set and Hurt retain configured strength. Hold follows live strength; Pulse captures rising-edge strength until it ends. Analog Reverse outputs 15 minus active strength, including 15 outside a pulse; disabled/dead/master-off still clear output.

Ramp linearly changes start to end strength over the configured duration, then holds the endpoint while triggered. Start/end support 0-15 and wheel steps of 1. Reverse, Hold/Pulse and pulse duration are ignored in Ramp mode; swap endpoints to reverse. Ending the trigger immediately outputs zero and resets the ramp, including a Move Set action ending early. Next activation starts again. All three destinations use the same ramp; other producers still merge by highest strength. New modules default to Selected surface only; saved face selections remain unchanged.

dashboard.sablelife.description_sensor: Detects targets or input signals and outputs a control signal.
dashboard.sablelife.description_navigati: Outputs redstone signals based on the target direction for turning and movement mechanisms; does not directly move or rotate the creature.
dashboard.sablelife.description_arena: Checks whether targets are within a marked arena.
dashboard.sablelife.description_armor: Use phase rules to increase or reduce damage received by the marked part or the whole creature.
dashboard.sablelife.description_melee: Damages targets in a marked area.
dashboard.sablelife.description_flame: Emits a stream of flame from the marked point.
dashboard.sablelife.description_gun: Fires fast projectiles from the marked point.
dashboard.sablelife.description_homing: Forms a hovering projectile pattern, then launches guided projectiles.
dashboard.sablelife.description_laser: Projects a damaging beam with aiming and tracking controls.
dashboard.sablelife.description_quake: Creates ground waves that damage and launch targets.
dashboard.sablelife.description_pull: Pulls targets within a configured area.
dashboard.sablelife.description_particle: Decorative Area, Point, Line, Ring or Sphere effects, with independent area/point marks.
dashboard.sablelife.description_trigger_: Plays a sound when its trigger activates.
dashboard.sablelife.description_loot: Configures rewards dropped by marked body parts.
core.sablelife.death_help: Cosmetic effects play once when health reaches zero, before delayed breakup. Duration 0 uses the particle's natural lifetime. Preview does not kill the creature.
core.sablelife.pattern_help: Choose the particle layout. Left click: next; right click: previous. Spread controls its size.
core.sablelife.vanish_help: Particles play at disappearing blocks after death delay, up to 16 locations per cleanup tick. Sound plays once. Preview uses the core position without removing blocks.
dashboard.sablelife.description_linear_m: Moves the connected Sable structure from a marked reference point, using Teleport or gradual Travel. Collision checks depend on the selected mode.
dashboard.sablelife.linear_help:
Angles are relative to the marked direction: positive horizontal turns right, positive vertical turns up. Teleport always checks the destination. Travel always checks terrain and stops at the last safe position. Full limb bounds are checked, so narrow gaps may be rejected. Toward target selects the nearest eligible target within search range, fixes its center at charge start and stops N blocks before it, measured from the marked movement point. Distance at or below N causes no movement. Target mode replaces fixed distance, face direction and angle offsets; it does not rotate the body. Teleport/Travel and existing obstruction rules still apply. Creative players can be included. Use target height defaults Off, keeping displacement horizontal; On uses the recorded target height for a 3D path. Force movement defaults Off. On skips terrain/body collision prechecks. Travel advances from frozen starting positions so contact pushback cannot erase progress. Destination chunks and world bounds still apply. Terrain is not destroyed; normal physics still applies after movement.

Continuous Travel can run with Auto facing or Signal turning. Fixed-direction Travel recomputes the marked part direction and angular offsets each tick, so backwards/strafe offsets rotate with the body. Distance is cumulative route progress and does not reset on turns. Gravity Travel measures actual core horizontal progress, excludes lifting/in-place rotation, and preserves gravity, step assist and end braking. Forced planned part positions rotate together without snapping to old offsets. Target-position mode still approaches its recorded charge-start endpoint, not the current target. Teleport pauses turning from charge through its completion tick. Active Signal turning wins over Auto facing; Hover anchor and recovering Gyroscope retain their priorities. Preview shows the initial route at the current heading, not later steering.
dashboard.sablelife.move_runtime_blocked: Movement blocked: terrain, border or unloaded area
dashboard.sablelife.flame_visual_help: Particle chooses the spray appearance and per-type size/lifetime; 0 lifetime covers the path. Effects apply on successful hits, subject to the damage interval. Damage and Burn remain separate; particles do not change the hitbox.
commands.sablelife.unconditional_help: Does not check the previous row. The module trigger and block type still determine when this row runs.
commands.sablelife.conditional_note: Conditional: previous row must succeed in this pass.
commands.sablelife.completion_help: Tab: complete / cycle candidates; Shift+Tab: previous; arrows or mouse: select.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_death_note: Kills nearby survival players when the countdown ends.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_force_return_n: Immediately returns the creature to center with full HP; overrides player punishment.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_countdown_help: Starts when the creature leaves the arena. Each nearby survival player gets a full countdown. Returning inside cancels it; player death is optional.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_mark_help: Area and point marks are saved separately. Area needs two points on one limb; other patterns share one marked face. Sneak-right-click air clears only the current mark mode.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_pattern_hel: Area uses its two-mark box; other patterns use a marked face origin. Start distance shifts the whole pattern along Direction; Ring lies perpendicular to Direction. Random/Even controls placement; density is particles per type. Sphere can fill its interior or surface. Ring height 0 keeps one ring; positive height extends a hollow cylinder along the selected direction. Density is shared over the cylinder surface, not multiplied per layer. Outward/inward propagation moves radially around each cross-section. Area/two-Mark and point patterns support additional length/width/height, 0â€“128 blocks, default 0. Length grows forward along the selected direction; width/height expand symmetrically, rotating with the marked part. Area adds to the original marked box. Point grows from its existing emission point into a box, line or plane. Zero preserves existing behavior. Preview and emission share the dimensions; Density still controls total particles. Other patterns keep their own dimensions. Visual only.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_spray_help: Spray births particles at the origin and moves them at the configured speed to Length. Lifetime 0 covers the full journey; a shorter custom lifetime cuts it off. Native friction and gravity do not shorten the path.
sound_timeline.sablelife.title: Sound timeline
sound_timeline.sablelife.open_help: Open the sound timeline: multiple sounds with independent start time, pitch, volume and range. MC/OGG tools are inside.
sound_timeline.sablelife.library_help: Left-click selects; double-click listens; right-click adds a layer. Duplicate sounds are allowed.
sound_timeline.sablelife.property_help: Times are relative to this event. Start 0â€“600s, pitch 0.5â€“2, volume 0â€“4, range 1â€“256 blocks.
sound_timeline.sablelife.duration_help: 0 plays naturally (BGM loops). A positive limit stops this layer at that time; fading happens within the limit. Dashed tails indicate unknown natural length.
sound_timeline.sablelife.natural: Natural length / BGM loop; timeline tail is symbolic.
sound_timeline.sablelife.cutoff: Ends at the configured playback limit.
dashboard.sablelife.melee_hit_limit_help: 0 = unlimited hits, still limited by Interval. Positive values cap successful hits per target during this continuous trigger window. Leaving/re-entering the area does not reset counts. Signal off, disable or reload starts a new window.
dashboard.sablelife.melee_offset_help: The first marked face defines forward. Positive horizontal turns right; positive vertical turns up in that face-relative plane. Angles rotate the entire box around its center and steer Start distance. The box keeps its size and follows the limb; Preview uses the same geometry.
dashboard.sablelife.melee_help: Damage and effects apply on successful contact. Interval is per target and per module. The hit cap is per continuous activation; 0 is unlimited.
core.sablelife.knockbackResistance_help: Reduces incoming module attack knockback and quake push/launch by this percentage. 0 = original force; 100 = no attack impulse. Independent of adaptive defense. Does not change damage, attraction, self movement, gravity or native structure collisions. Mouse wheel: Â±5%.
core.sablelife.defense_note: Defaults 100 / 80% / 1s: 200 incoming DPS gives 50% reduction (~100 DPS); 1,000 gives 80% (~200 DPS). Steady rates after the window fills, not a hard damage cap.
core.sablelife.defense_help: Default Off. Threshold 0.1â€“1,000,000 HP/s; cap 0â€“100%; window 0.1â€“10s. Above the threshold, reduction rises with incoming DPS. The proposed hit is included; rejected or fully blocked hits do not count. Healing does not count. Changing these settings resets the rolling window.
core.sablelife.defenseThreshold_help: The incoming DPS at which protection begins, after armor. Lower = earlier/stronger protection; higher = more damage allowed. It is not a per-hit cap. At 200 sustained DPS with threshold 100, target reduction is 50%, unless limited by Maximum reduction.
core.sablelife.defenseMaximum_help: The highest adaptive reduction allowed, not a constant reduction. 0 = no adaptive mitigation. 80% leaves at least 20% of incoming damage: 1,000 sustained DPS can still deal about 200 DPS. Thus the DPS threshold is not a hard damage cap.
core.sablelife.defenseWindow_help: DPS = damage in the last N seconds / N. Short windows react more strongly to brief bursts and forget them sooner; long windows need more accumulated damage and retain it longer. 100 damage in a 1s window = 100 DPS; in 0.5s = 200 DPS. This is a measuring window, not an immunity duration.
manual.sablelife.title: Operating manual
manual.sablelife.schema_note:
Read current values and ranges in the module editor. Hover controls for help; some appear only in the selected mode. Sound layers use the sound timeline.

These chapters describe ordinary Heart Core modules. Other core types and server switches may restrict them.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.usage: Start with an ordinary Heart Core in Creative mode. It gives an assembled Sable structure health and module-controlled behavior. Follow the six steps below to make one simple arrow attack.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.setting:
Choose a core

Heart Core: practice in Creative mode. Survival editing is disabled by default; administrators can enable it.

Survival Heart Core: editable in Survival mode, with Energy costs for health and paid abilities. Read its chapter before activating.

Redstone Core: runs supported controls on an assembled structure, without creature health or life activation.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.example:
Minimal arrow setup

Core: ordinary Heart Core in Creative mode, assembled with one core across all connected parts.

Module: Arrow launcher, enabled. Aiming: Straight. Trigger: Always. Start distance: 1 block. Mark: an outward-facing block face on the structure. Keep other settings at their defaults.

Preview should place the muzzle outside the body. After life activation, the module fires along that direction. To aim at a moving target later, change the aiming mode and configure target selection separately.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.trouble:
If nothing happens, first check that the structure is assembled and has only one core across its connected parts. Then check four things: the creature is active, the module is enabled and allowed by the server, any required mark is valid and connected, and the trigger is satisfied. For channel-controlled actions, also check the channel and wireless master switch. Paid Survival Heart Core actions need enough Energy. A Redstone Core does not need life activation.

Release before changing locked settings; controls intended for live use remain available. Sneak-right-click activates a dormant Heart Core but does not release an active creature.

Use an empty hand to open the core; holding a block can disguise it instead. Release keeps saved settings but does not restore removed blocks or give death rewards.
manual.sablelife.core.usage:
Core settings affect the whole creature: health, regeneration, protection, targeting and death effects. Use the Survival Heart Core chapter for that core's fixed rules and Energy costs.

Health regenerates after the configured quiet period following damage. It cannot revive a dying or dead creature. Configure drops through Whole-body loot on the module dashboard.
manual.sablelife.core.settings:
Health and rewards
Healing per second = fixed regeneration + maximum health x regeneration percent / 100. Both use the same post-damage delay. XP Points gives a fixed amount; XP Levels adds levels to the collector, like /experience add levels. Converting units uses cumulative XP from level zero.

Interaction
Survival interaction defaults Off. Off locks supported devices and their open inventories for Survival/Adventure players while active; Creative is unaffected. On permits interaction, while mining and placement retain separate rules. Core status remains accessible. Dormant/released builds and Redstone Cores use normal rules; third-party remote controls may need adapters.

Adaptive defense
Defaults: Off, 100 HP/s threshold, 80% maximum, 1-second window. Damage is measured after part armor, before adaptive reduction. Sustained 200 DPS approaches 50% reduction; 1,000 DPS reaches the 80% cap. These are not a hard DPS cap or invulnerability window.

Other defense
Knockback resistance defaults 0%; 100% blocks supported Melee/Shockwave/Earthquake impulses, not their damage. Attraction, self-movement, gravity and native collisions are unaffected. Full heal on player kill defaults Off; it requires an attributed Survival/Adventure player death. Totems and later environmental or damage-over-time kills do not count.

Terrain breaking
Collision terrain breaking defaults Off. When enabled: contact delay 0, support protection On, visual debris On, block drops Off. It breaks at actual block shapes, not empty gaps in the bounding box, before Travel step assist. Other Sable structures are not removed. Containers may release contents even with block drops Off. Server budgets apply.

Protected blocks
Up to 128 block IDs or #tags. Load preset merges 20 common natural blocks without duplicates. Inventory samples consume no items; Shift-click adds, right-click removes, Confirm commits and Cancel discards. Non-block items are ignored. Grid entries show full IDs on hover; tags use books and itemless blocks use barriers.

Targets
Target Whitelist & Factions excludes listed usernames from automatic targeting, including All; names ignore case and may be offline. Rename entries when players rename. It does not protect against stray projectiles.

Each creature has one faction; players may join several. Public factions are open; private factions need a creator/operator invitation and acceptance in Details. Invites use UUIDs and online/previously seen names. Select a faction to assign this creature; None clears its assignment. Leaving as a player does not remove existing creatures. Only creators/operators manage privacy, members, deletion and alliances.

Faction creation
Non-operators can own one faction by default. maximumFactionsPerPlayer in the server config changes this limit; 0 removes it. Operators (permission level 2+) bypass the personal limit, while the global 256-faction limit still applies. Existing factions are retained, and joining multiple factions remains allowed. Deleting an owned faction frees a personal slot.

Alliances are direct and require both factions to agree; A-B and B-C do not ally A-C. Either side may end its alliance. Same-faction/allied creatures skip automatic targeting. Friendly Fire covers incidental Sable Life damage within a faction; allied damage requires both sides to allow it. Other mods' weapons are outside these switches. Factions grant no editor, mining or interaction access; unknown copied UUIDs create no alliance.

Priority and Owner
Priority ranks eligible targets when selecting/reselecting: Nearest, Players First, Sable-Life Creature First or Other mob first. Existing locks and multi-target rules remain. Owner is optional and case-insensitive; Owner mode selects only that player, even if whitelisted, and waits if unavailable. Other automatic attacks and direct module damage exclude the owner. Owner grants no editing access and can appear in death messages.

World and death
Void death height checks the active core's world-space center: strictly below it kills regardless of defense. Default: dimension minimum Y (-64 Overworld; 0 Nether/End). Dormant builds and Redstone Cores are unaffected. Right-click Apply restores the default.

Force chunk loading defaults Off; On follows active/dying connected parts. Release, core removal, cleanup completion or switching Off releases tickets. Limits: 256 target chunks per creature, 1,024 server-wide.

Death delay is 0-60 seconds. Death effects play at zero health; vanish effects after the delay. Each has its own sound mix; Restore resets only that stage. Core names support standard & formatting and &#RRGGBB within 64 characters. Direct module kills use the launch-time styled name; later environmental/status deaths use vanilla attribution.
manual.sablelife.core.example:
1. Open Core settings and set maximum health and regeneration.

2. Configure death and vanish effects on their separate pages. Choose each stage's particle pattern and sound mix, then Preview it. Preview closes the menu so you can see the effect; reopening that core returns to the same settings page.

3. If you want protection against sustained high damage, open Defense settings. Try threshold 100 HP/s, maximum reduction 80%, and window 1 second.

4. Activate the creature. Compare isolated hits with sustained attacks, then use Release before changing settings that are locked while active.
manual.sablelife.core.troubleshooting:
Adaptive reduction decreases smoothly as recent damage leaves its measurement window. Changing defensive settings clears the temporary damage statistics.

Physically removing the core is not a normal damage hit and is not prevented by adaptive defense.

For cleanup while away from the area or after closing the world, see Death delay and chunk unloading.
manual.sablelife.triggers.usage: A trigger decides when an enabled module runs. You can trigger one module directly, or trigger a Move set that schedules several modules together.
manual.sablelife.triggers.settings:
Always runs while the Heart Core is active, or while an assembled Redstone Core is operational. Mark redstone reads power at the marked input. Internal wireless reads this core's channels; external wireless uses the red/blue frequency items.

For an action scheduled by a Move set, choose the Move set trigger. For a reaction to damage, choose Hurt and configure its response mode, signal duration and cooldown.

Attack Interval and a sound layer's Start time are separate settings. One controls repeated attacks; the other delays audio playback.
manual.sablelife.triggers.example:
1. Select Trigger when hurt on an independent attack.

2. Open its hurt settings and choose response, duration and cooldown.

3. For a combination, instead set action modules to move set and the controlling Move set to Hurt.

4. Independent Hurt modules may run alongside that combination.
manual.sablelife.triggers.troubleshootin:
A short trigger can allow only one shot or hit. Hurt cooldown limits new reactions, not the attack's own interval.

Internal wireless reads channel output; External RX reads received input. Channel numbers are local, while external red/blue items choose the frequency. See Wireless Channels for the four connection routes.
manual.sablelife.sound_timeline.usage: Use the shared sound editor to combine several sound layers. It is used by sound modules, death and vanish effects, and BGM.
manual.sablelife.sound_timeline.settings:
Each layer has Start, Pitch, Volume, Range, Limit and Fade settings. Limit 0 lets an effect sound finish naturally, or lets BGM use its normal looping behavior.

A positive Limit stops playback after that many seconds. Fade uses the final part of that time: with Limit 1.5 and Fade 0.5, fading starts at 1 second and playback stops at 1.5 seconds. Fade 0 stops immediately at the limit. If Fade is longer than Limit, fading uses the whole playback period. A sound that ends naturally is not extended by fading.

Dashed tails on the timeline do not show measured file lengths.

Scroll over Start, Pitch, Volume, Limit or Fade to adjust it by 0.1. Range changes by 8. Fade accepts 0â€“600 seconds.
manual.sablelife.sound_timeline.example:
1. Open a sound button; search the left library. MC and OGG tools are inside this page.

2. Double-left-click a library or selected sound to listen. Right-click a library sound to add it, then add another layer.

3. Set starts to 0 and 0.4 s; adjust each pitch/volume.

4. Preview one layer or the mix, stop and return.
manual.sablelife.sound_timeline.troubles:
Closing preview stops its queue. Effect tails may finish after an attack phase, but disabling/deleting their source cancels them.

Custom OGG resources must be present on listening clients. Hearing range is not attack range.
manual.sablelife.retaliation.usage: Use a Hurt-triggered Move set for a coordinated reaction, with an optional independent Hurt module for an extra response.
manual.sablelife.retaliation.settings: Set the controlling Move set to Hurt and configure its response there. Set each action it schedules to the Move set trigger. A separate Hurt-triggered action uses its own cooldown, independently of the Move set.
manual.sablelife.retaliation.example:
1. Add and mark an attack and Trigger sound.

2. Set both to move set triggers and add them to one Move.

3. Set the Move set to Hurt and choose a one-response mode and cooldown suitable for the sequence.

4. Optionally add a separate marked Hurt attack.

5. Damage once, then rapidly again; verify both response cooldowns.
manual.sablelife.retaliation.troubleshoo: If a required action is missing or invalid, the whole reaction is unavailable. A canceled Hurt Once reaction does not retry continuously; it needs a new damage event.
manual.sablelife.survival_core.usage: The Redstone Core is a survival-craftable control core with a purple crystal. It controls an assembled Sable structure without giving it life or health. It is a different item from the Energy-powered Survival Heart Core.
manual.sablelife.survival_core.settings:
Supported modules are Move set, Signal logic, Pulse sequence, Wireless redstone, Target sensor, Target alignment, Auto facing, Signal turning, Gyroscope, Hover anchor, Linear movement, Visual Effects, Distortion trail, Particle effects, Item display, Trigger sound and Block Interaction. They are enabled by default; administrators can disable them in [modules.redstoneCore]. Sound, BGM and combat/life modules remain unavailable.

Assemble the structure with exactly one core across all connected parts. Wireless Master controls output. Supported triggers are Always, marked-point power, internal channel and external receive. Compatible actions can also use Move set.

Move set always ignores target, distance, cone, visibility and health conditions. Priority, Weight, Move cooldown, Move time, Rest and Consecutive repeats still apply.

Linear movement is restricted to collision-checked Travel, with Force movement unavailable. Gravity and step assist keep their own Travel settings. Old unsupported settings remain stored but cannot run on this core.
manual.sablelife.survival_core.example:
1. Craft one core: redstone block / redstone torch / redstone block; repeater / amethyst shard / comparator; redstone block / lever / redstone block.

2. Place it in a body and assemble using the normal Sable assembly workflow.

3. Empty-hand right-click to configure. Add Wireless redstone, mark an outlet or choose Frequency Item.

4. Choose Always for continuous output, or connect an internal/external channel trigger. Use Master to pause. No life activation is needed.
manual.sablelife.survival_core.troublesh:
Not assembled, duplicate core or Master Off stops output. Newly placed duplicates are rejected; duplicates introduced by assembly, merge or reload suspend output until removed.

Match frequency items and choose the correct trigger/channel. Copy and reload preserve unsupported settings in a disabled state.
manual.sablelife.move_set.settings:
Each move has conditions for target distance, health range and line of sight. Eligible moves are then selected by Priority or Weight. Forward reference defines the front used by directional checks. Cooldown limits how often a move can repeat; Rest adds time between moves.

The Move set itself stores the conditions and timeline. It does not need a separate dispatcher, and existing saved rules load automatically.

Separate Move sets select and run independently. If they schedule the same module, their action windows are combined: the module stays triggered while at least one window is active. It still has one runtime and its own interval. A second overlapping window does not duplicate, queue or restart it.

Ignore conditions when selecting moves is a switch in the outer Move set properties, below Edit move set. It is Off by default. Turn it On for behavior such as target-free mechanical wandering. It skips target, distance, cone, line-of-sight and health checks for every move in that controller.

While that switch is On, target, health, distance, cone and line-of-sight controls are gray. Priority, Weight, Move cooldown, Move time, Rest after move and Consecutive repeats remain editable. Their saved values are kept. Cooldowns, busy time, Rest and repeat settings still apply, and invalid actions or server-disabled modules still prevent selection.
manual.sablelife.move_set.example:
1. Add two attack modules, give them valid marks, and set both to the Move set trigger.

2. Add a Move set module and open Edit move set.

3. Add one move, then add the two attacks as actions on its timeline. Start the second action at 0.5 seconds and set a suitable duration for each action.

4. Configure the move's conditions and timing. Choose a trigger for the controlling Move set, then activate the creature to test the sequence.
manual.sablelife.move_set.troubleshootin:
A missing, disabled, disconnected or unmarked required action makes the entire move unavailable. If a required action becomes invalid during the move, remaining scheduling is canceled. The controller can still select other valid moves; if none are valid, it waits. It does not skip the broken action and continue the same move.

Wireless redstone and Command can be valid without a mark when using their supported unmarked behavior.

Shared modules and channels are not reserved for one controller. For example, action windows of 0â€“3 seconds and 2â€“5 seconds keep a shared module triggered continuously from 0â€“5 seconds. Use separate module instances and channels for independent behavior. Overlapping sequence outputs on one channel use the highest strength.

Hover over the small ? beside the move status to see broken references, including the module name, number, first affected action and reason. Repeated references to the same module appear once. The list updates after you repair them.
manual.sablelife.wireless_redstone.setti:
Destinations
Marked faces, external red/blue frequencies and this core's internal channel can be combined. Mark-only needs no frequency items; internal/external output needs no mark. New marked output uses the selected surface only.

Strength and timing
Fixed strength uses Power. Hold follows the trigger; Pulse lasts its duration after a rising edge. Reverse swaps zero/strength: reversed Hold is high while idle; reversed Pulse drops for the pulse then returns high, even with a held trigger. Disabled/invalid modules, dormant/dead cores or Master Off output zero.

Follow input preserves 0-15 from Internal wireless, External RX or Anchor power; Always/Move set/Hurt use configured strength. Hold tracks changes; Pulse snapshots the rising-edge strength. Analog Reverse uses 15 minus strength, including 15 outside a pulse.

Ramp
Start to End rises/falls linearly, then holds End while triggered. Ending input immediately outputs zero and resets it. Reverse, Hold/Pulse and pulse duration do not apply; swap endpoints to descend. All destinations share the ramp.

Internal channels and latch
Choose an enabled Sequence-controlled internal output channel; 0 is unbound. Shared sources combine by highest strength, including ramps. Separate input/output channels to avoid feedback.

For a lasting phase, enable Latch on a Wireless output channel and send a transition pulse. Reset channel clears it and takes precedence; 0 means none. Input must go low before relatching. Runtime latch state is not saved: trigger it again after reload.
manual.sablelife.wireless_redstone.examp:
1. Add Wireless redstone and set its trigger to Move set. Set its internal output to channel 10.

2. In Wireless, enable channel 10 and configure it as Sequence-controlled with Internal output.

3. Schedule Wireless redstone as an action in a Move set. While that action is active, the channel supplies the module's output.

4. For example, keep an Armor module on Always and make one of its rules read channel 10 while powered. No Pulse sequence module is needed between them. Marked-face and external outputs can run at the same time.
manual.sablelife.wireless_redstone.troub:
Internal output needs a bound, enabled Sequence-controlled channel. Channel 0 disables that destination. Without any configured destination, the module emits no signal.

Deleting a channel unbinds matching outputs and adjusts later references. Portable presets require internal output channels to be assigned again.

If an inverted signal never seems to go low, check for another source holding the same channel or frequency high.
manual.sablelife.command.settings: Each command row uses Impulse, Repeat or Chain behavior. A Conditional row runs only if the immediately preceding row succeeded during the same pass. Repeat interval controls how often Repeat rows run.
manual.sablelife.command.example:
1. Open Edit commands and add a blank row.

2. Enter say hi. Use Tab for completion, then click Save command.

3. Choose Impulse, enable the module and activate its trigger.

4. Add a Conditional Chain row to test a command that depends on the previous row succeeding.
manual.sablelife.command.troubleshooting: Saving a command does not execute it. Check your permissions and the server's command settings if it does not run. Commands execute at the moving core's position and do not need a mark.
manual.sablelife.melee.settings:
Mark two corners on the same rigid body to define the attack volume. Start distance shifts the volume. Horizontal and vertical angles rotate the volume and its offset direction around its center.

Hit limit applies separately to each target during one continuous activation. A value of 0 allows unlimited hits, still spaced by Interval. Burn time is 0â€“30 seconds, default 0. Only a successful damage hit ignites the target; a blocked hit does not.

Length extension adds space along the first marked face's direction. Width and height add to the full dimensions, divided equally between both sides. All three extensions default to 0 and accept 0â€“128 blocks. The extended area follows the part and its configured angles.

Use Preview to align the attack volume with the visible weapon. Changing an item display's scale does not automatically resize the damage area.
manual.sablelife.melee.example:
1. Mark two corners on the same rigid body to cover the intended attack area.

2. Set Hit limit to 3 and choose an Interval between hits. Adjust Start distance, angles or size extensions as needed.

3. Use Preview to align the area with the weapon or limb.

4. Keep the trigger active while a target enters and leaves the area. Each target can take up to three successful hits during that activation.
manual.sablelife.melee.troubleshooting: Leaving and re-entering the area does not reset a target's hit count. Ending the module's activation does. A short Hurt Once trigger may end before repeated hits can occur.
manual.sablelife.flame.settings:
Speed controls how fast the flame travels, Width controls its spread, and Range controls its reach. Use Start distance to place the outlet clear of the structure.

Open Particle to choose normal fire, soul fire or a mixture of supported particles. Each selection has its own size and lifetime. Lifetime 0 lets the particles cover the journey.

Effect applies status effects on successful hits. Direct Damage and Burn are configured separately.

To leave an area after impact, select a Persistent area damage template. Configure its damage and particles there; enable Ignite on contact in the template if it should keep targets burning after contact.

Start distance moves the launch point along the original selected direction first. The horizontal and vertical firing angles then change the stream's direction at that point; they do not rotate the positioning offset. Both default to 0. Horizontal accepts -180 to 180 degrees, with positive values turning right. Vertical accepts -90 to 90 degrees, with positive values turning up.

For example, Start distance 2 places the outlet two blocks ahead along the original direction. A vertical angle of -45 then sends the stream downward from that outlet. In Preview, cyan shows the positioning line and yellow marks the launch point. A Summoned weapon uses its own launch position and direction.

Fan spreads sideways around the firing direction. Fan angle sets the opening (5â€“180Â°), and End radius sets the vertical half-thickness at the curved outer edge.
manual.sablelife.flame.example:
1. Mark the intended outlet on the structure.

2. Open Particle to select the flame appearance, size and lifetime. If needed, open Effect and add Slowness with a duration and level.

3. Set Burn to 0 if the attack should not ignite targets. Damage, burning and potion effects are separate settings.

4. Use Preview to check the outlet and direction, then trigger the module against a test target. Start with a moderate Width.
manual.sablelife.flame.troubleshooting:
Particle size does not set the damage hitbox. A short particle lifetime can make the visual end before the attack reaches its full range; use 0 to cover the configured journey.

Status effects require successful hits and follow the same hit interval. If firing seems intermittent, check the trigger, direction and Interval. Older blue-fire and size settings are converted automatically.
manual.sablelife.particles.settings:
Marks and size
Area uses two corners; Point/Line/Ring/Sphere share a separate single mark. Start distance offsets the origin. Area/Point extensions add forward Length and symmetric Width/Height (0-128); the volume rotates with its part. Density stays the total amount, not per layer. Other patterns use their own sizes.

Pattern and motion
Ring height 0 makes a circle; positive height makes a hollow cylinder along Direction. Random/Even and Sphere Inside/Surface control distribution. Line/Ring/Sphere can propagate outward/inward at blocks per tick; Life 0 covers the path. Motion trail fills movement/rotation gaps; Only while moving gates emission. Density applies to each selected type.

Particle picker
Color, Life and Size are per selection. Effect/Instant effect/Entity effect/Dust and bundled Sable types support RGB; Presets restores appearance while retaining your custom color. Block/item payloads are unsupported. All are cosmetic.

Bundled Sable shapes
Search sable: electric arc, smoke, energy mote, branching lightning, streak spark, expanding/contracting rings, crescent shard, soft fog and starburst. Life 0 uses native lifetimes; Size 1 is the baseline. Arcs are camera-facing flashes, not lightning joining two marks; their bends change every 2 ticks. Bright particles do not light nearby blocks.

Rings face the camera around their own centers, not attack boundaries. Fog grows upward; sparks drift outward without supplied velocity. Fixed starburst stays upright; Starburst chooses and keeps a random angle. Old configurations retain Fixed. Iris uses the standard translucent renderer; without it, soft alpha. Color/lifetime/size/animation work in both.
manual.sablelife.particles.example:
1. Choose Sphere, mark one point, set a radius, and select Random and Inside. Use Preview to see the distribution.

2. Switch to Area and mark two corners on one rigid body. Switching back to Sphere keeps the separately stored point mark.

3. For a tube, choose Ring with Radius 2, Ring height 8, direction Up and Density 32. Preview shows three circular sections and the side edges. Raise Density if the particle wall looks too sparse.

4. Use the particle picker to adjust Color, Life and Size separately from the pattern dimensions. Line also supports placed or spray modes.
manual.sablelife.particles.troubleshooti:
Clearing a mark affects only the current mark mode. High density and multiple selected types increase particle output and can reach shared visual budgets.

Controlled propagation is not shortened by native friction or gravity. A custom lifetime shorter than the journey still makes the particle disappear early.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.setting:
New modules default to Internal wireless. Bind a channel and supply its signal to start movement. Saved modules keep their trigger and step cooldown.

Direction and target
Fixed distance follows the mark and angle offsets. Toward target chooses by core priority within search range, then records its position at charge start; it does not chase later movement or turn the structure automatically. No target means waiting.

Stop before target measures mark-to-target-center distance, not a gap between hitboxes. Use target height Off keeps current height/horizontal distance; On uses the recorded height and 3D distance. Creative-player inclusion is separate. Owner mode selects only the named owner, even if whitelisted, and waits if unavailable; other target modes exclude that owner.

Teleport or Travel
Teleport moves after charging; Travel moves gradually. Both check loaded destinations and world borders. Force movement (default Off) skips collision prechecks, not those checks; forced Travel maintains its planned route until normal physics resumes at the end. Charge/departure/arrival effects are separate.

Gravity Travel
Default Off. On drives connected parts horizontally while retaining relative limb motion, vertical velocity and rotation; vertical aim and Force are ignored. Only actual horizontal progress counts. A blocked run times out; ending brakes horizontal motion without suspending the build.

Step assist
Travel only, gravity On or Off; default Off. Grounded parts can lift the whole build together over 0.3 seconds, braking vertical velocity. Default height 1 block (0.1-2), cooldown 0.3 seconds. Clear the obstruction and regain clear ground contact before another step; limbs cannot stack lifts. There is no headroom guarantee, and sparse/rotated builds may tip. Gravity resumes after a gravity-assisted lift; without gravity, route height stays raised until movement ends. Lift does not count as forward progress. Terrain breaking runs first.

Turning and Preview
Travel can steer with Auto facing or Signal turning; fixed-direction routes turn with the structure without resetting distance. Target routes keep their recorded destination. Teleport pauses turning through its completion tick. Active Signal turning takes precedence over Auto facing; Hover anchor/Gyroscope retain their priorities. Preview shows the current heading, not future steering or a predicted landing.

The destination preview outlines individual block shapes in green when clear and red when blocked. Very large previews use a bounded block scan and retain a bounding box for unfinished parts. Collision checks still use each connected body's bounding box.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.example:
1. Mark a starting face. Choose Teleport, a short fixed distance and zero angles, then Preview on flat ground.

2. Switch to Travel and set a speed for gradual movement. Test clearance before adding gravity, step assist or turning.

3. For target movement, choose Toward target, a target type and a search range. Set Stop before target to 2. A target center 10 blocks from the mark gives 8 blocks of movement, subject to collision checks.

4. Target movement does not turn the structure. If its marked front points north and the target is south, it moves south while still facing north. Use Auto facing first if it should turn toward that target. In a Move set, leave enough time for turning before starting movement.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.trouble:
Collision checks allow a small ground-contact tolerance, not embedding in walls. Every connected rigid body's contact-adjusted enclosing box is checked against terrain collision shapes and nearby collision shapes of other Sable bodies (their enclosing boxes only select candidates). Ordinary living-entity hitboxes are not part of this precheck.

These enclosing boxes can include empty corners around rotated or sparse parts, so movement can stop before a visible block touches the obstacle. Travel approaches the nearest allowed position and stops. Teleport cancels if a required path or destination check fails. The target stopping distance does not override collision checks.

Stop before target measures the marked point to the target's center. When movement ends, normal physics resumes; this module does not keep the structure suspended or locked in place.
manual.sablelife.arena.usage: Manage the creature leaving a fixed arena, with nearby-player warnings and optional punishment or return.
manual.sablelife.arena.settings:
Arena rules
Mark a fixed world center and set the horizontal radius. The leaving countdown starts when the creature leaves, not when players leave. Nearby-player death defaults On; Force return with full health defaults Off and takes precedence. No-nearby-player return is separate.

With Iris active, respawn text and progress use a world-positioned HUD overlay after shader rendering, retaining distance scaling. This does not change normal text displays.
manual.sablelife.arena.example:
1. Mark a clear arena center and set the radius.

2. Disable nearby-player death while testing. Enable force return if you want the creature to return instead of dying outside the arena.

3. Move the creature outside the radius and observe its warning and countdown.

4. If using Automatic respawn, record the structure and test a full death/respawn cycle before using the encounter. Check the template's ground clearance, not just the center point.
manual.sablelife.arena.troubleshooting:
The arena center stays fixed in world space. Force return keeps the creature's height; it does not automatically place its feet on the ground.

If punishment does not occur as expected, check the nearby Survival-player range and whether force return is enabled. For respawn placement, also check the anchor clearance and loaded chunks described in this chapter.
manual.sablelife.homing.settings:
The marked face defines the formation and fan directions. Use Offset and Height to position the hovering projectiles. Deployment and charging finish before they launch.

Target filters, tracking and lifetime control pursuit after launch.

Area damage on impact can use a Persistent area damage template. Projectiles from the same salvo that hit the same patch refresh its duration rather than stacking damage. No impact area appears during deployment, charging or flight before contact.
manual.sablelife.homing.example:
1. Mark the launch face and choose Arc (n).

2. Set both formation rotations to 0, then view the Preview from in front of that marked face.

3. Choose eligible targets and configure tracking. Trigger the module and watch deployment, charging and launch in order.
manual.sablelife.homing.troubleshooting: A formation viewed from above can look different from its front view. Confirm the marked face before changing rotations, and check the target filters if projectiles do not acquire a target.
manual.sablelife.mortar.settings:
Target selection, speed and launch angle determine the projectile's arc. The chosen warning color is visible from the start of the warning. Explosion damage and block damage are separate settings.

Area damage on impact can use a Persistent area damage template. Configure residual burning with Ignite on contact in that template, and select flame particles separately.

The impact particle picker changes appearance only. Color, Life and Size apply to the selected particles; Size changes each particle, not the damage or warning radius. Spread can follow the damage radius or use an independent radius of 0â€“32 blocks.

Count is shared across the selected impact particles. Count 1 places a particle at the center; radius 0 places all of them there. An empty selection emits no impact particles. Flight particles are configured separately.

Custom item rotation X/Y/Z accepts -180 to 180 degrees and defaults to 0. These are local model offsets relative to flight: custom gun bullets and mortar shells follow their velocity, including the mortar arc. Arrow camera-facing mode applies offsets relative to the viewer instead. Rotation changes appearance only; it does not change launch direction, trajectory, collision or Energy cost.
manual.sablelife.mortar.example:
1. Mark the launch face and choose a target mode.

2. Set a warning color that is easy to see, then test in open terrain.

3. Check that the whole arc clears the structure and nearby obstacles before increasing the range.
manual.sablelife.mortar.troubleshooting: If shots miss or collide early, check the target range, launch angle and clearance along the arc. A large projectile may need a greater Start distance.
manual.sablelife.navigation.usage: Target alignment outputs directional redstone signals for a movement or aiming mechanism that you build. It does not move or turn the Sable structure directly.
manual.sablelife.navigation.settings:
Choose a target range, forward reference, tracking mode, dead zones and target lock. Reverse redstone directions swaps Left/Right, Up/Down and Forward/Backward without changing signal strength.

You can assign six internal outputs: Left, Right, Up, Down, Forward and Backward. Channel 0 leaves a direction unbound. Left/Right and Up/Down are angular corrections and drop to zero when aligned. Forward/Backward indicate bearing; Forward can reach 15 when aligned.

Create and enable the channels in Wireless. Choose Sequence-controlled internal output, or external transmission if needed, and leave Latch Off. These outputs preserve their actual strength; the channel's fixed-strength and pulse settings do not reshape them. Sources sharing a channel combine by highest strength.

Losing the target or trigger, disabling or deleting the module, or cleanup removes this module's contribution to the signal. Deleting a channel unbinds matching references and adjusts later ones.

Owner follows only the player named in this core's Owner setting, including Creative players and names on the exclusion list. Other target modes exclude the owner. The player must be online, in the same dimension and within search range; otherwise no target is selected.
manual.sablelife.navigation.example:
1. Mark a face that points toward the structure's front. Choose a target type, search range and tracking settings.

2. Assign the directional outputs to your turning or movement mechanism, then test both horizontal and vertical alignment.

3. For internal steering, send Left to channel 1 and Right to channel 2. Configure Signal turning to read those same internal channels and mark the same front face. Connect Up and Down in the same way for pitch.

4. Feed these outputs directly to preserve their analog strength. A Wireless redstone relay in fixed-strength mode replaces the input strength with its configured strength. The turning controller may read a change one game tick later.
manual.sablelife.navigation.troubleshoot:
This module supplies control signals. Use Linear movement for direct displacement, Auto facing for direct target tracking, or Signal turning for direct rotation from signals.

If your mechanism moves incorrectly, check its wiring, front mark and direction assignments.
manual.sablelife.health_phase.settings:
Open the phase editor to add up to 64 rows. Each row has its own enable switch, health range, output channel, strength, output mode and pulse duration. The lower health bound is exclusive and the upper bound is inclusive.

Hold keeps the output active while health stays in the row's range. Enter emits a pulse when health enters that range. The module's outer trigger must be active for either mode to run.

Overlapping rows can output together. If they share a channel, the highest strength wins. Use an enabled Sequence-controlled channel configured for internal output or external transmission. Channel 0 leaves the output unbound.
manual.sablelife.health_phase.example:
1. Add three Hold rows: 70â€“100% on channel 1, 40â€“70% on channel 2, and 0â€“40% on channel 3.

2. Configure and enable those output channels in the Wireless editor. At exactly 70% health, row 2 applies; at exactly 40%, row 3 applies.

3. To test Enter instead, change a row to that mode and enter its range. Additional hits inside the same range do not restart its pulse. Leaving the range or losing the outer trigger cancels it; entering again can emit a new pulse.
manual.sablelife.health_phase.troublesho:
The lower bound must be below the upper bound. Check the selected row's output status in the editor.

Editing or disabling another row does not restart this row's pulse. Deleting an output channel unbinds rows that used it and adjusts later channel references.

Normal world saves keep the rows and their outputs. Presets keep ranges and modes but require outputs to be assigned again. Older single-phase settings load as the first row.
manual.sablelife.sequence.settings: Open the sequence editor to add output steps and waiting periods. Once runs one sequence per input pulse; Repeat runs again while powered. Stop on low controls whether losing input stops playback. The reset source and channel determine which signal restarts it.
manual.sablelife.sequence.example:
1. Open the sequence editor and add two steps with different output channels and durations.

2. Configure matching receivers on those channels.

3. Test Once with a short input pulse, then test Repeat with a held input. Check Stop on low if the sequence should stop when input ends.
manual.sablelife.sequence.troubleshootin: Check both the reset source and reset channel. An internal channel number and an external receiver with the same number are not the same input.
manual.sablelife.sound.settings:
Approach, hurt and ambient events each have their own sound mix. Set their detection ranges, cooldowns and ambient timing to control when playback begins.

For block-contact sounds such as footsteps, use Trigger sound instead.
manual.sablelife.sound.example:
1. Open one event's sound mix and add the desired layers.

2. Preview the mix, then set that event's range, cooldown or timing.

3. Activate the creature and trigger that event, such as approaching it or dealing damage.
manual.sablelife.sound.troubleshooting: Hearing range is separate from the event's detection range. An empty sound mix is silent. See Sound combinations for layering, playback limits and fading.
manual.sablelife.trigger_sound.settings:
Configure the ordinary trigger sound with its playback mode, cooldown and repeat interval. Each sound layer has its own Start, Pitch, Volume and Range.

Block contact sound is separate. It has an enable switch, sound mix, one of six local directions, a detection distance and a cooldown. While the module is triggered, entering contact plays that mix once. Remaining in contact does not loop it, and its cooldown is independent of ordinary trigger playback.

You can use both mixes together. Clear the ordinary mix if only contact sound is wanted. Contact direction and Preview follow the selected local face as the structure turns.
manual.sablelife.trigger_sound.example:
1. Mark the sound origin and add layers to its ordinary sound mix.

2. Choose Move set to schedule it with an action, or Hurt for an independent damage reaction.

3. Test the mix and trigger. For footsteps or impacts, enable Block contact sound and test its direction, distance and separate cooldown instead.
manual.sablelife.trigger_sound.troublesh: The action window is not an automatic sound cutoff. Set a layer's Limit if playback must end after a specific duration.
manual.sablelife.bgm.settings: Choose when the music starts, how far away players can hear it, and its fade behavior. Each layer keeps its own delay and playback limit. Without a limiting duration, BGM uses its normal looping behavior.
manual.sablelife.bgm.example:
1. Add music layers and Preview the mix.

2. Configure the start behavior, range and fade.

3. Activate the creature, then approach and leave its music range to check the transition.
manual.sablelife.bgm.troubleshooting: BGM needs no mark. When several creatures are nearby, their music sources compete rather than all playing independently. Each listening client needs any custom audio resources.
manual.sablelife.loot.settings:
Whole-body and part loot use the same editor. The left side contains 27 sample slots and your inventory. The right side contains quantity, chance or weight, mode and draw count.

In Chance mode, every populated slot is checked independently. In Weighted mode, each draw selects from entries with positive weights. Quantity sets the dropped stack size separately. Whole-body weights accept 0â€“100; part weights accept 0â€“1000.

Click a sample with an empty cursor to select it. Change values with the fields, buttons or mouse wheel: Chance changes by 5, Weight by 1 and Quantity by 1.
manual.sablelife.loot.example:
1. With an item on the cursor, left-click a sample slot to copy the stack or right-click to add one. Without a carried item, right-click removes one. Clear deletes the sample.

2. Shift-click an inventory item to copy it into the first empty sample without consuming it. Shift-left-click or Shift-right-click a sample raises or lowers its rule value.

3. Select a sample and set its quantity and chance or weight. Custom item names and components are kept. Your ordinary inventory controls remain available.
manual.sablelife.loot.troubleshooting:
While the creature is active, the loot editor is read-only. You can select samples to inspect their settings.

Samples are configuration, not storage: they cannot be taken out, collected or thrown. Chance mode does not use Draws. Part drops and whole-body drops are separate reward settings.
manual.sablelife.armor.settings:
Open the phase-rule editor to add rules. Each has an internal or external signal source, input channel, damage modifier, and powered or unpowered condition.

Whole body changes which parts the module protects. Off applies to the separately marked part. On covers all connected parts of this creature and needs no mark. Switching scope keeps the same rules.

The module's outer trigger must be active, including when scheduled by a Move set. With no matching rule, damage is unchanged. If several rules match, the lowest modifier wins; they do not stack. Channel 0 or a missing channel leaves a rule unbound.

Modifiers accept -100% to +1000% and change by 5 per wheel step. A rule set to apply while unpowered stops applying when its input turns on, then resumes when it turns off. Global adaptive defense is applied after these modifiers.

Survival Heart Cores cap reduction at 90% (-90 modifier). Each percentage point costs 1 Energy per active second at the default server rate: 50% costs 50/s, 90% costs 90/s. Each active armor module is billed independently, including when no damage is received. Old stronger rules are limited to -90; ordinary Heart Core limits are unchanged.
manual.sablelife.armor.example:
1. Keep Armor on Always. Add rules for channel 1 at -100%, channel 2 at -50%, and channel 3 at +50%.

2. Use Health phase to hold the appropriate channels for immunity, reduced damage and vulnerability. If channels 1 and 3 overlap, -100% wins.

3. For immunity that pauses during a signal, add a -100% rule on channel 4 and select Apply while unpowered. The rule resumes when channel 4 turns off.

The -100% examples above are for ordinary Heart Cores. A Survival Heart Core stops at -90% and charges Energy while reduction is active. Use its module estimate and server rate when planning a timed defense.
manual.sablelife.armor.troubleshooting:
A part-scoped module needs a valid mark; Whole body does not. Disabled rules and rules with missing or unbound channels do not apply.

Deleting a channel unbinds rules that used it. Presets keep values and conditions but require input channels to be selected again. Normal saves and structure copies keep the rules. Changing scope does not erase them.

Older whole-body single-value settings are not converted into phase rules. Recreate those settings in the rule editor.
manual.sablelife.sensor.settings:
Detection radius is 1â€“256 blocks, default 12. Shape, radius, inner radius, front end radius and direction define the detection area. Front end radius appears only in Forward cone mode; its mouse-wheel step is 1 block. Target type and line of sight determine which entities count inside it. Only loaded targets can be detected; the sensor does not load remote chunks.

The marked face outputs weak redstone power at strength 15, so a lamp at that output can light up. It does not emit through all faces. To route an internal signal, select an enabled Module output channel; 0 leaves it unbound. Red/blue frequency items add an external output. Channel strength settings do not change the marked output's strength of 15.

Invert signal powers the outputs when no target is detected and clears them when a target is detected. A disabled or inactive module, or one without an active trigger, outputs nothing.

Owner selects only the player named in this core's Owner setting, even if that name is also on its exclusion list. It can detect that player in Creative mode. The player must be online, in the same dimension and inside the detection area. If there is no matching player, there is no target; it does not choose someone else. Other target modes exclude the owner.
manual.sablelife.sensor.example:
1. Mark the sensor's output face on the structure.

2. Choose a detection shape, target type and range, then use Preview to inspect the area.

3. Connect the marked redstone output, an internal channel or external frequencies to your receiver.

4. Activate the module and move an eligible target into and out of the detection area.
manual.sablelife.sensor.troubleshooting: Targets outside the detection shape are ignored. If line of sight is required, an obstruction can also exclude them. Check detection first, then check the output routing separately.
manual.sablelife.laser.settings:
Beam and damage
After charging, beam length and width determine contact. Damage count Ã— damage interval determines the firing duration; the firing interval separates bursts. A zero sweep angle fixes that axis.

Sweep speeds
In fixed-direction mode, a nonzero horizontal or vertical sweep angle reveals its own speed control (0â€“720Â°/s). The default 0 preserves the old automatic timing. Positive speeds are independent of damage timing: start at one edge, sweep toward the other, then hold if reached early. Slow sweeps may finish partway through the angle. Negative angles reverse that axis. Each burst starts again from the first edge.

The default continuous beam follows the moving muzzle, supports RGB color and interpolates between visual updates each frame. The legacy style keeps its particle beam. Extra particles are optional; their spacing is 0.25â€“32 blocks (default 4), with at most 64 sample positions per beam per tick and the shared player visual budget. Smaller spacing makes them denser. Particles already emitted retain their normal lifetime and may leave trails. Visual settings do not change hit width or damage timing.

Terrain cutting
Break blocks defaults Off. Clear whole line removes breakable centerline blocks; Cut forward advances from the first obstruction at Breaking speed (default 16 blocks/s), checked every firing tick, independently of hit interval. Allow enough burst time to reach the distance.

Own connected parts are skipped; unbreakable/protected blocks and unloaded chunks stop cutting. No block-item drops are created, but container removal may release contents. Trigger loss/burst end stops cutting. Charge and Preview do not break terrain.

Origin and impact
Start distance offsets along the original direction; angles/sweep turn the beam there, not the offset. Positive horizontal turns right, vertical up. Target modes aim from that point; Summoned weapon supplies its own origin/direction. Preview uses cyan positioning and a yellow origin.

An optional Persistent area damage template uses supporting ground for entity contacts or the impact face for terrain. Its shape, duration, particles, damage and burning are configured in the template.
manual.sablelife.laser.example:
1. Mark the beam origin and choose an aiming mode.

2. Start with a short charge and beam length. Use Preview to check the origin, angles and path.

3. Configure charge and firing sounds separately, then trigger the module against a test target.

4. If testing block cutting, use Fixed direction and a nearby breakable wall first.
manual.sablelife.laser.troubleshooting:
A short trigger may end before charging finishes. Beam width controls collision; particle size only changes appearance.

Automatic targeting needs an initially visible target. Use Fixed direction to start cutting directly into a wall. During firing, tracking can follow an acquired target that moves behind a breakable wall.

Laser cutting shares a limit of 1,024 removed blocks per world tick. Remaining obstructions wait for a later firing tick.
manual.sablelife.ground_strike.settings:
Mode, radius, range, ray count or random count determine the strike positions. Start distance, wave delay and step control progression; the warning appears before damage.

Area damage on impact can use a Persistent area damage template. Configure the area separately, including dimensions, angle, duration, particles, damage and residual burning.

The falling item's orientation defaults to Face camera. Fixed orientation applies world-space X, Y and Z angles in XYZ order, each from -180 to 180 degrees. These angles rotate the item model without changing its vertical fall, range or damage. Each cast keeps the appearance it had when released. For a vanilla sword, try X=0, Y=0, Z=-135 degrees, then adjust for your model.

Falling item size accepts 0.1â€“32 blocks and uses the model's longest edge. It affects appearance and visibility culling, not the damage radius. Older configurations use their former projectile diameter as the visual size.

The impact particle picker also changes appearance only. Color, Life and Size apply to particles without changing damage or warning radius. Spread follows the damage radius or an independent radius of 0â€“32 blocks. Count is shared across selected particles; Count 1 stays at the center, and radius 0 centers all particles. An empty selection emits no impact particles. Flight particles are separate.
manual.sablelife.ground_strike.example:
1. Mark an origin if the selected release mode needs one. Choose a strike mode and warning color.

2. Preview a short range and test the strike positions.

3. Adjust the falling item's size and orientation if needed. Increase the number of rays or area only after the basic pattern works.
manual.sablelife.ground_strike.troublesh: If strikes appear in the wrong place, check the placement and target modes first. Warning time delays the hit; it is not the repeat interval.
manual.sablelife.quake.settings: Choose Line, Ring or Area, then a marked origin or target-foot origin. Range, Width, Speed and wave gap control the wave's shape and propagation. Grounded-target settings determine whether airborne targets can be hit.
manual.sablelife.quake.example:
1. Mark an origin if required and choose Line or Ring.

2. Use a modest range and warning time, then Preview the shape.

3. Trigger it against a target standing on the ground. Adjust the grounded-target rules if airborne targets should also be affected.
manual.sablelife.quake.troubleshooting: Grounded-target rules can exclude targets in the air. Wave travel time and the interval between attacks are separate settings.
manual.sablelife.pull.settings:
In marked-point mode, Start distance places the pull center ahead of the marked face. In target-position mode, an eligible target supplies a fixed cast center; no mark is needed and Start distance is ignored. Radius determines which targets are affected around that center. Stopping distance brakes them near the center; it does not extend detection range.

Warning time runs before active pulling. Pull duration, strength and speed control the action. Default warning and pulling sounds are beacon activation and beacon ambience.

For spherical attraction, the outer shell shows the capture area. Repeated particle streams converge from its surface toward the center. The cross marks the pull point and the small ring shows stopping distance. Select particles and RGB colors for the streams, or leave the selection empty to use dust in the Warning color.

Target-position mode can release at one target or, with Multiple target On, at each eligible target up to 64. Centers are recorded when warning starts and do not chase later movement. Search range and effect radius are separate. One batch shares a cooldown, and no eligible target means no cast.

For a directional funnel, use Mark mode and configure Length, Start radius, End radius and horizontal/vertical angles. Start distance positions it before the angles are applied. Equal radii make a cylinder. Target-position mode remains spherical.

Stable suction gradually reduces sideways drift and compensates for gravity during active pulling. It does not disable gravity permanently or bypass collision and speed limits.
manual.sablelife.pull.example:
1. Mark a point and choose eligible targets. Start with modest strength and speed.

2. For a sphere, set Radius and Stopping distance, then Preview and test one target.

3. For a funnel, choose the directional shape and set Length, Start radius and End radius. Position it with Start distance, then adjust horizontal and vertical angles.

4. Test Stable suction if targets drift sideways or fall away from an angled pull path.
manual.sablelife.pull.troubleshooting: Check the target range, detection shape and any line-of-sight requirement. Collision can stop a target from reaching the center, and different entity types may respond differently to motion. Stable suction does not pull through solid obstacles.
manual.sablelife.pulse.usage: Shockwave applies radial damage and knockback around a marked origin or sampled target position. Its visual expansion does not delay the hit.
manual.sablelife.pulse.settings:
Radius, Damage and Knockback control each pulse. In marked mode, Start distance offsets the origin and Interval controls repetition.

Fixed boundary ring draws a ring at the edge. Outward sphere expands from the release center to Radius over 0.05â€“10 seconds, default 0.5. This expansion is cosmetic: damage and knockback resolve immediately, with no extra hits as it expands.

Choose center and boundary/wave particles separately, including size and lifetime. Empty a group to hide it. Outward particles last at least long enough to reach the boundary.

Target-position release needs no mark. Multiple target Off uses one eligible target; On releases at each eligible target, up to 64. Positions are sampled afresh for each release. Search range and effect radius are separate, and one batch shares a cooldown. No eligible target means no pulse.
manual.sablelife.pulse.example:
1. Choose a marked origin and a small Radius and Knockback.

2. Preview the boundary, then trigger against one nearby target.

3. Compare Fixed boundary ring with Outward sphere. The visuals differ, but both apply their hit immediately.
manual.sablelife.pulse.troubleshooting: Check the target filter and Interval if no hit occurs. Knockback does not guarantee movement through obstacles, and the visual expansion is not a moving damage wave.
manual.sablelife.arrow.settings:
Projectile and aim
Choose appearance, speed, count/scatter and residual time. Visual size, damage, explosion and block breaking are separate. Arrows retain gravity.

Straight uses the mark. Target position samples visible eligible targets at firing; one uses core priority, Multiple target sends a full volley to each (up to 64). Search range defaults 64, maximum 256, independent of flight range. No target means no shot; there is no homing or movement prediction.

Launch point
Start distance offsets along the original direction. Angles/fan change flight from that point without rotating the offset; positive horizontal turns right, vertical up. Summoned weapon supplies its own origin/direction. Cyan Preview lines show positioning; yellow marks the muzzle.

Impact
Landing sound is independent of Fire sound: untouched default uses native arrow audio, a custom mix replaces it, empty is silent. Entity-hit audio is unchanged; explosive block impacts may also play it. Settings survive projectile save/reload.

Optional Persistent area damage uses supporting ground for entity hits or the terrain impact face. Configure its shape/duration/damage/burning in that template; none selected means no extra area.

Custom item visuals
Always faces camera suits flat icons such as snowballs. Local X/Y/Z rotation defaults 0, accepts -180 to 180 degrees. Ordinary orientation follows flight; camera-facing offsets follow the viewer instead. These change only the model, not trajectory, gravity, hitbox or Energy cost.
manual.sablelife.arrow.example:
1. Mark the firing face and use Preview to check the direction.

2. Set Start distance to place the launch point clear of the structure, then choose the flight speed and aiming mode.

3. Configure Fire sound and Landing sound separately. Preview the landing mix, then shoot a nearby wall to test it.

4. Test Target position mode with an eligible target in search range if you want aimed shots.
manual.sablelife.arrow.troubleshooting: Clearing Landing sound does not mute Fire sound or explosions. Epic Fight ordinary Guard excludes projectile damage; native Parrying allows projectiles with an eligible weapon.
manual.sablelife.gun.settings:
Shots and aim
Speed, count and Interval control volleys. Visual/collision sizes, explosion damage and terrain breaking are separate.

Straight uses the mark. Target position samples visible eligible targets at firing. One uses core priority; Multiple target sends a full volley to each (up to 64). Search range defaults 64, maximum 256, independent of flight range. No target means no shot. Bullets do not home or lead targets.

Launch and visuals
Start distance offsets along the original direction to clear the body; angles/fan change flight without rotating that offset. Positive horizontal turns right, vertical up. Summoned weapon supplies its own origin/direction. Cyan Preview lines show positioning; yellow marks the muzzle.

Custom item X/Y/Z rotation is local to flight, -180 to 180 degrees, default 0. It changes appearance, not aim, trajectory, collision or Energy cost. Mortar models similarly follow their arc; camera-facing arrows use viewer-relative offsets.

Impact area
Select a Persistent area damage template for an extra area: supporting ground on entity hits, actual impact face on terrain. Set shape, duration, particles, damage and burning in the template. No template means no extra area.
manual.sablelife.gun.example:
1. Mark the firing face. Start with one projectile and a short range.

2. Use Start distance to clear the structure, then Preview the direction.

3. Activate the trigger and check the shot. Increase the count or add effects after basic firing works.
manual.sablelife.gun.troubleshooting: Immediate collision usually needs clearance or Start distance; check direction before increasing damage.
manual.sablelife.module_management.usage: Manage abilities as virtual modules inside the core. Purple modules handle signals, red modules handle attacks, and yellow modules provide functions. Renaming a module keeps its original type; hover its sidebar entry to identify it.
manual.sablelife.module_management.setti:
Add and edit
+ Add browses All/Signal/Attack/Function/Presets. Search localized names, English names or IDs; select and Add, or double-click. Apply names/numbers with Enter or the checkmark; mode buttons save immediately. Wheel steps depend on the field.

Find and reorder
Sidebar search spans pages and accepts names, types or original numbers; #12 matches module 12 exactly. Clear search to see all. Arrows beside Add reorder modules.

Copy or remove
Copy inserts an independent module after the original, retaining marks/rules/channels/action references but no runtime. Recheck those bindings before using both. Locked editing or the module limit prevents copying. Disable keeps settings; Delete requires a second click.
manual.sablelife.module_management.examp:
Copy an existing Arrow launcher named Left cannon to make a Right cannon. Rename the copy, then mark a block on the right side: copying initially keeps the original mark. Disable the copy if you want to compare the two configurations without deleting either.

Save a preset to reuse the configuration in another build. A preset needs new marks and bindings; it does not carry the old body with it.

Use the Data Copier to transfer a whole core configuration: right-click to copy when empty, right-click a dormant core to paste, or Shift + right-click to copy new data. All three core types follow their editing permissions. Pasting replaces settings and requires new marks; Energy and current paid health are not copied.
manual.sablelife.module_management.troub:
A red number field contains an invalid value; use the displayed limits. Renaming does not break module references, but disabling or deleting an action required by a Move set can make the whole move unavailable.

Server module switches are under [modules.heartCore], [modules.redstoneCore] and [modules.survivalHeartCore]. Setting one to false hides it from Add and suspends existing instances while keeping their settings. Re-enable it to restore operation. These switches cannot give a core an unsupported ability. For a module that still does not run, use the checklist in Getting Started.
manual.sablelife.marking_system.usage:
A mark selects a block, face or area of the Sable structure. A mouth mark can supply a Flamethrower's origin; two corners can define a Melee volume. It does not mark a player or mob as an attack target.

Ordinary marks follow their part's position and rotation. Arena uses a fixed world center. Blueprint generation can use a fixed world point or follow a marked part. Block Interaction marks the reference part, then searches its configured world or structure area. Marking does not move blocks.
manual.sablelife.marking_system.settings:
Point mark: right-click one block face on a connected part. The selected face also supplies the mark's direction.

Area mark: Melee and Particle Area use two block corners on the same rigid body. Each axis can span up to 32 blocks, including both corners. Two articulated parts can be connected to the same creature without being the same rigid body.
