Particle Area stores its two-corner mark separately from the single mark used by point patterns.

For Target alignment, choose a horizontal face that points toward the structure's front. For Arena, choose a terrain or structure point to use as its fixed world center.

Core modules do not need a mark. Wireless redstone can transmit externally without a marked output face.
manual.sablelife.marking_system.example:
1. Select the module and click its Mark button. The editor closes and a selection hint appears.

2. For a point mark, right-click the intended block face. For an area mark, right-click two corners on the same rigid body. A successful selection returns you to the dashboard.

3. Check the mark's status and use Preview to inspect the direction or volume.

4. To replace it, click Mark again and complete a new selection.

5. To cancel without changing the saved mark, press Esc or sneak-right-click a block.

6. To clear the saved mark, start marking again, aim into the air and sneak-right-click. This clears the current mode's marks and reopens the dashboard.
manual.sablelife.marking_system.troubles:
Clearing works only during mark selection, with no block in reach of the server's selection ray. Sneak-right-clicking a block cancels the selection instead.

A second corner on another rigid body, or beyond the allowed size, is rejected. Choose a valid corner or cancel. Selection expires after two minutes and can also end if permissions or configuration change.

A required mark becomes invalid if its part is destroyed or disconnected. Clearing it returns the module to Not marked and disables its Preview.

For particles, clearing the Area mark does not erase the separately stored point mark.
manual.sablelife.preview_system.usage: Use Preview to check an origin, direction, volume or path before activating the creature. Geometry previews do not fire attacks or move the structure. Particle previews may emit decorative particles.
manual.sablelife.preview_system.settings:
A normal mark preview lasts about five seconds and is visible only to the player who requested it.

Preview can be unavailable if a required mark is missing, its part is disconnected, or you lack permission. Some modules have a dedicated editor or do not use a mark preview at all.

Wireless redstone can transmit externally without a mark even when its marked-output Preview is unavailable. A valid mark does not activate the module by itself.

Mark and volume previews use continuous outlines in their own colors. Entity hitbox preview is white. Blueprint and natural-spawn previews can also show block models; large templates may show only bounds because of the projection limits. A visible projection is not proof that placement is allowed.
manual.sablelife.preview_system.example:
1. Apply settings and complete the required mark.

2. Click Preview; inspect the front face, area or movement path in the world.

3. Reopen the dashboard and adjust direction, Start distance, angles or range if needed.

4. Repeat Preview, then separately activate the creature and satisfy its trigger for a real test.

5. For sounds or Core death/vanish effects, use their own Preview controls.
manual.sablelife.preview_system.troubles:
If Preview is gray, first check whether that module needs a mark. A module with an unmarked output destination may still be able to run.

A red Linear movement path or destination indicates a collision problem, not a trigger problem.

For an area mark, inspect the full rotated volume rather than only its center.

Effect previews demonstrate visuals and audio. Previewing a death effect does not kill the creature.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_trail_help: Interpolates particle emission along the moving/rotating body path. Off emits only at its current position. Different from Only while moving; stationary bodies look the same.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_motion_only: Only emits when the marked body moves or rotates. This controls when to emit; Motion trail controls whether to fill gaps.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_propagation: Line/Ring/Sphere: Pattern default keeps placement (Line spray still moves outward). From center travels to Length/Radius; reverse travels from the endpoint/edge to center. Speed is blocks per tick. Native friction/gravity do not shorten the path. Lifetime 0 covers the journey; a shorter custom lifetime cuts it off. Drift and sphere interior fill apply to static placement.
dashboard.sablelife.description_auto_fac: Directly turns the connected creature toward its selected target while active. The marked face defines its front.
dashboard.sablelife.auto_facing_help:
Mark the front face. Default: nearest selected target within 64 blocks, 180 deg/s, horizontal turning. Vertical tracking also tilts the entire creature. Terrain/other machines block turning; large bodies may turn more slowly. Teleport takes precedence; only the first available facing controller operates. If vertical rotation is blocked, safe horizontal turning continues.

Can turn during continuous Travel; directional drive follows heading. Paused during Teleport.
dashboard.sablelife.facing_state_front_i: Mark a side face, or enable vertical tracking
dashboard.sablelife.facing_state_blocked: Rotation blocked by terrain / body unavailable
manual.sablelife.auto_facing.settings:
Choose a target type and search range. Turn speed accepts degrees per second and defaults to 180.

Horizontal tracking turns the structure around its vertical axis. Vertical tracking can also tilt the whole structure. The Creative-player option allows eligible Creative players to be selected.

Line of sight defaults Off. On requires a visible eligible target; the visibility check ignores the creature's own connected structure.

Owner follows only the player named in Core settings, even if that name is on the exclusion list. It still respects this module's Creative-player option. Other target modes exclude the owner. No online matching player in range means no target.
manual.sablelife.auto_facing.example:
1. Add Auto facing and mark a face that points toward the structure's front.

2. Choose a target type, range and turn speed. Preview the front direction.

3. Select Always, activate the creature, and move an eligible target around it.

4. Test vertical tracking separately if the whole structure should also tilt toward targets above or below it.
manual.sablelife.auto_facing.troubleshoo:
With Line of sight On, no visible eligible target means no turning. Horizontal mode needs a front face with a horizontal direction; use vertical tracking for other orientations.

Collision check defaults On. Terrain and structure bounds can block unsafe rotation. Blocked vertical rotation can still allow a clear horizontal turn. Off skips those checks and turns through intersecting terrain at the configured speed.

Teleport takes priority over turning. Otherwise, the first available Auto facing module controls it, unless a higher-priority controller is active. Target alignment only outputs signals for a mechanism you build.

Continuous Travel can turn with Auto facing or Signal turning. Fixed-direction Travel updates its direction with the structure; target-position Travel keeps its recorded destination. Active Signal turning takes precedence over Auto facing. Hover anchor and a recovering Gyroscope can also pause turning. Preview shows the current heading, not later steering.
dashboard.sablelife.mark_auto_facing_poi: Right-click the front face. Horizontal tracking needs a side face; enable vertical tracking for top/bottom fronts. Esc cancels; sneak-right-click air clears.
sound_timeline.sablelife.row_help: Left-click selects; double-click listens using this layerâ€™s settings, without its start delay.
core.sablelife.restore_help: Restore this stageâ€™s default particles, pattern, count/spread and primary sound mix. Death instant: fireworks and blast sound. After delay: disappearance smoke, no sound. Does not change health, Death delay or the other stage.
dashboard.sablelife.navigation_invert_he: Swap left/right, up/down and front/back output faces while preserving strength. Example: left 8 becomes right 8. No target remains silent; disabling the module or ending its trigger shuts outputs off.
dashboard.sablelife.facing_state_vertica: Vertical rotation blocked; horizontal tracking continues
core.sablelife.xp_units_help: Points: 0â€“30,970 raw XP, dropped as ordinary XP orbs. Levels: 0â€“100; the player collecting the level reward orb gains that many levels directly, like /experience add <player> <amount> levels. Switching display units uses cumulative XP from level zero; applying a value changes the amount. Existing pending death jobs retain their saved reward mode.
control.sablelife.unassembled: Assemble this body to enable control
control.sablelife.duplicate: Only one core per connected body; remove the extra core
control.sablelife.ready: Redstone control ready; no life activation needed
control.sablelife.paused: Redstone control paused by master switch
tooltip.sablelife.redstone_core: Harmless redstone control. Assemble one core per body; no life activation needed.
dashboard.sablelife.control_audio_help: Redstone Core has no combat or hurt events. BGM plays while triggered for nearby listeners; combat-start settings are inactive. Shared settings are retained for copying to a Heart Core.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_target: Checks this target type at selection time; does not control aiming or movement.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchFar: At least one target must be within this distance.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchCool: Starts when chosen; prevents selecting this move again until it ends.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchWeig: Weight 20 is twice as likely as weight 10 among eligible moves.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchBusy: Waits at least this long, and longer if its sequence is still running.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchRest: After the move and its sequence finish, wait before choosing another move.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_phaseUpper: This constructâ€™s current HP percentage must be at or below this value. Together with minimum HP, controls when the move is eligible; for example maximum 50 and minimum 0 enables it at half health or below.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_phaseLower: This constructâ€™s own HP percentage must be above this value; 0 is the lowest boundary. Use it to assign moves to health phases. This is not the targetâ€™s HP.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchNear: Target must not be closer than this distance.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchCone: 360 accepts all directions; smaller angles require a target in front.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchFron: Defines forward relative to the core and rotates with it. Used only when target angle is below 360Â° to decide whether a target lies in the allowed cone. It does not change projectile direction.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_lineOfSight: Targets hidden behind walls do not make this move eligible.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchRepe: Avoid repeat chooses another eligible move if possible; allows this move when it is the only eligible one.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.usage: Death delay is tracked by a world-owned death job, independently of the core block ticking. Leaving the area does not revive a dying creature or restart its delay.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.setting:
The death countdown continues while the server is ticking, even if the creature's chunks unload or a multiplayer player logs out.

With Force chunk loading Off, cleanup and loot/XP wait for the chunks they need to be loaded naturally. With it On, the active or dying connected structure stays loaded, and required reward chunks are held until settlement, within the loading limits.

Closing a single-player world, stopping the server or pausing its ticks saves the remaining delay. Time spent offline is not deducted.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.example:
1. Set Death delay to 60 seconds and kill the creature.

2. Wait 20 seconds, then teleport away for 45 seconds while the server keeps ticking. On return, the delay has already expired. Cleanup and reward settlement proceed when the required chunks are available; the 40-second remainder does not restart.

3. Compare this with closing the single-player world after the first 20 seconds. Reopening resumes with about 40 seconds left, regardless of how long you were away.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.trouble:
Void-height death uses the same death effects, delay, cleanup and loot/XP locations; it does not rescue or move rewards to safe ground. Height detection requires the living core to tick.

An unloaded corpse may remain saved until it can be cleaned safely; this is pending cleanup, not renewed life. Large bodies can take several ticks to clean.

Loading applies to world-space body coverage, not only the core block or Sable storage coordinates. The settings page reports target chunk count or an exceeded limit.

Loot/XP settlement is recorded to avoid duplicate rewards. Chunk loading cannot make a stopped or paused server continue ticking.
core.sablelife.force_chunk_help: On: keeps an active or dying Heart Core and its connected body loaded, following movement. Off, Release, core removal or completed cleanup releases only its own loading tickets. Default Off. Max 256 target chunks per creature, 1024 server-wide. This cannot run a stopped/paused server.
core.sablelife.void_death_help: An ALIVE Heart Core below this world-space Y dies regardless of armor/adaptive defense. Default: current dimension minimum build height (usually -64 in the Overworld). Strictly below, not equal. Normal death delay, effects and loot remain unchanged. Integers -2048 to 2048; scroll Â±1. Right-click the apply button to restore the dimension default.
dashboard.sablelife.description_sphere_b: Charge a sphere at a fixed point ahead of the marked face, then explode once. Separate charging/blast particles and sound mixes; optional effects and block destruction.
dashboard.sablelife.sphere_blast_help: Center = marked block center + face direction Ã— (0.55 + Start distance + Distance from start). Sphere freezes in world space when charging begins. Radius defines spherical damage; each target is hit once per explosion. Cancelling the trigger or losing the mark cancels charging. Block destruction defaults Off and uses vanilla explosion resistance when On. Preview causes no damage. Charging particles travel to the sphere center; Charging speed controls movement independently of Charge time (default 2 blocks/s). New modules use Small flame + Firework. At explosion, both the charging and explosion selections expand from the center to Blast radius at fixed 12 blocks/s. Short charges can truncate slow travel; damage radius is unchanged. At target samples the nearest eligible target within Target search range when charging begins, then fixes that world position. No Mark is required in that mode. Target-position release needs no Mark. Multiple target Off selects the nearest eligible target; On releases at each eligible target, up to 64. Sphere Blast and Attraction freeze centers at charge/warning start; Area Pulse samples fresh centers per release. No target means no cast. Search range and effect radius are independent; a batch shares one cooldown. Mark mode retains its existing behavior.
manual.sablelife.sphere_blast.settings:
Marked point places the sphere ahead of the marked face. Start distance offsets the starting point, then Distance from start places the sphere farther along that direction. Radius controls the spherical damage area.

At target needs no mark. It records eligible target positions when charging begins. Multiple target Off selects one using the core's target priority; On charges a sphere at each eligible target, up to 64. Search range and effect radius are separate. One batch shares a cooldown. No eligible target means no cast.

The sphere stays at its recorded world position during charging; it does not follow the structure or target. A target can leave before the explosion.

Charging defaults to Small flame and Firework particles. They travel toward the center at Charging speed, default 2 blocks per second. Speed does not change Charge time. The explosion ends the charging particles, so a short charge can cut slow travel short.

At explosion, selected charging and explosion particles expand to Blast radius at a fixed 12 blocks per second. This animation does not change the damage radius.

Charging and explosion have separate particle selections and sound mixes. Hit Effects are separate, and block destruction defaults Off.
manual.sablelife.sphere_blast.example:
1. Mark a firing face. Try Start distance 0, Distance from start 8, Radius 4, Charge time 2 seconds and Interval 5 seconds.

2. Preview the positioning line and sphere. Configure charging and explosion particles and sound mixes separately.

3. Activate the module and observe the charge followed by one explosion.

4. In a Move set, give the action enough time to complete charging.
manual.sablelife.sphere_blast.troublesho:
Losing a required mark or trigger, or disabling the module, cancels pending charging. The positioning line causes no damage along its path.

The attack only runs at loaded destinations and does not load remote terrain. Each explosion damages each eligible target once rather than adding a duplicate vanilla hit.

Block destruction uses vanilla TNT resistance rules. It does not guarantee removal of every block inside the damage radius.
dashboard.sablelife.description_slash: Launches traveling crescent blades from a marked face. Configure their size, speed, range, fan spread, angles, appearance and sounds.
dashboard.sablelife.slash_help: Length spans the blade sideways; width is its depth along flight. Angle offsets steer the launch; blade rotation tilts its plane. Multiple blades spread evenly across the fan centered on the offset direction. RGB defaults white. Particle mode uses the particle selection. Speed is blocks/s. Each blade hits each target once; different blades may each hit it. Terrain stops the center path; no block destruction. Sound mix begins at launch. Preview is harmless. Interval measures release-to-release time; earlier blades keep flying while later volleys launch. Trigger/mark loss stops new releases, not launched blades. Hurt Once releases one volley. Death/Release clear flight. Up to 256 blades per module; at that limit, new releases wait without deleting existing blades. Release sound plays once per volley, regardless of blade count. Separate Flight sound loops at each moving blade and stops when that blade disappears. Duration 0 loops until flight ends; explicit row durations still apply. Either sound can be empty.
manual.sablelife.slash.settings:
Blade and aiming
Length/Width set span/depth; Speed and Range set flight. Count/Fan spread blades symmetrically; Blade rotation tilts the plane. Choose RGB or particles. Interval is between releases, so volleys may overlap in flight (up to 256 blades per module).

Straight uses the mark. Target position samples visible eligible targets at release; one uses core priority, Multiple target sends a full volley to each, up to 64. Search range (default 64, maximum 256) is separate from flight range. No target means no release. Blades do not home or lead targets; angle offsets still apply.

Impact and blocking
An optional Persistent area damage template appears on supporting ground for entity hits, or the actual impact face for terrain. Set its shape/duration/damage/burning in that template. Ignite target is separate (default Off, up to 30 seconds), can work on an accepted zero-damage hit and does not apply vanilla fire status to mechanical creatures.

Can be blocked defaults Off. On allows frontal vanilla shields and supported Epic Fight guards/parries; rear hits land. Blocking prevents direct damage, ignition, effects and impact area for that defender, without removing the blade.

Launch and sound
Start distance offsets along the original direction; angles/fan change flight, not that offset. Positive horizontal turns right, vertical up. Summoned weapon supplies its own origin/direction. Preview uses cyan positioning and a yellow launch point. Release sound plays once per volley; Flight sound follows each blade until it ends. Duration 0 loops the flight layer; a positive duration limits it. Either mix may be empty.
manual.sablelife.slash.example:
1. Mark the launch face. Try length 4, width 0.5, speed 16 blocks per second and range 24.

2. Preview the direction and blade size. Set Count to 3 and Fan to 60 degrees for three flight paths. Angle offsets change their shared heading.

3. Configure Release sound and Flight sound independently. Add any hit effects you need.

4. Trigger the module directly or schedule it in a Move set. Each volley plays one release mix; each flying blade has its own flight mix.
manual.sablelife.slash.troubleshooting:
The blade checks the space swept between positions to reduce missed hits at high speed. Each blade can hit a given eligible target once; different blades can each hit that target.

A blade's launch position and direction are fixed in world space after release. Later structure rotation does not steer it. Terrain on its center path stops it, and targeting excludes targets hidden behind walls. It does not destroy terrain.

Losing a required mark or trigger stops new launches. Already launched blades continue flying. Hurt Once releases one volley; death or Release clears active blades.

At 256 active blades per module, further launches wait for space without deleting existing blades. Release audio begins at the launch position and supports delayed layers.
dashboard.sablelife.rgb_help: Open the shared color picker: drag the square for saturation/brightness and the rainbow strip for hue. Precise RGB values update automatically. Confirm saves once; Presets returns to preset selection; Cancel keeps the original setting.
dashboard.sablelife.facing_collision_hel: On: terrain/body bounding boxes can block rotation, with horizontal fallback if pitch is blocked. Off: skip rotation collision checks and force turning, even while intersecting terrain. Line of sight remains a separate target selection setting.
dashboard.sablelife.pull_stop_help: Distance in blocks from the target center. Pull slows down near this distance and brakes inward movement; it does not teleport or lock the target.
module_picker.sablelife.name: Preset name
module_picker.sablelife.failed: Could not save preset (limit or file error)
module_picker.sablelife.portable: Save applied settings. Marks and module references must be set again after adding.
module_picker.sablelife.delete_help: Click twice within 2 seconds to delete the selected preset. Built-in modules cannot be deleted.
manual.sablelife.module_management.prese:
Presets

Use Save preset beside Delete module, enter a name, then confirm. Presets are saved in the client configuration and can be reused across worlds. They keep applied module settings, sound layers, particles and status effects; marks, arena centers and other module references need new bindings.

Duplicate names receive a number suffix. The preset list has its own sorting arrows, and deletion needs a second click to confirm. Players hearing custom audio still need the corresponding files on their clients.
language_picker.sablelife.title: Select language
language_picker.sablelife.help: Switch Minecraft language now without restarting. Keep the current module and property page.
dashboard.sablelife.description_item_dis: Displays a chosen item model on a marked body point.
dashboard.sablelife.item_display_help: Copies an item without consuming it; uses its handheld model, as homing projectiles do. Base position is the marked face center, 0.55 blocks from block center. XYZ offsets and X/Y/Z rotations use the marked body axes and follow that limb. Size sets the modelâ€™s longest dimension. Always display ignores signal and life activation, but still needs an enabled module and valid mark. Empty selection shows nothing. Preview outlines its maximum size; no collision, damage or item drops.
display_item.sablelife.title: Choose displayed item
manual.sablelife.item_display.usage: Display a selected item at a marked body point. This is a cosmetic function and creates no entities, collision, damage or collectible items.
manual.sablelife.item_display.settings:
Choose an item in the sample slot. Its item data is copied without consuming it. The display uses the same handheld-model rendering as homing projectiles, including model-based weapons.

Size sets the model's longest dimension from 0.05â€“32 blocks. X/Y/Z offsets use the marked part's local axes and accept -64 to 64 blocks. Local X/Y/Z rotations accept -180 to 180 degrees and are applied in XYZ order. The item follows its marked part.

Always display defaults Off. In that mode, the creature must be active and the module's trigger must be satisfied. On allows display even while dormant and ignores the trigger, but still requires an enabled, server-allowed module and a valid connected mark.

Administrators can allow this optional module on Redstone Cores; it is enabled there by default. Preview shows the maximum model extent, not a damage hitbox.
manual.sablelife.item_display.example:
1. Add Item display and choose a sword in Displayed item.

2. Mark the intended hand face.

3. Adjust size, XYZ offset and the three rotations; Preview its extent.

4. Turn Always display On to inspect while editing, or leave it Off and activate its trigger.

5. Save preset if you want to reuse the appearance; mark again on the new body.
manual.sablelife.item_display.troublesho: No item, disabled module or lost/disconnected mark means no display, even with Always display On. Ordinary item textures remain ordinary models; this does not invent a new 3D model. Custom assets must exist on viewing clients. Unloaded bodies are not force-loaded for this feature.
dashboard.sablelife.display_hidden: Hidden: check item, mark, enable and trigger
dashboard.sablelife.move_runtime_no_targ: No eligible movement target in range
core.sablelife.name_help: Supports &0â€“&f colors, &l bold, &o italic, &n underline, &m strikethrough, &k obfuscated and &r reset. Example: &c&lKilling Machine. Hex: &#FF5555. Formatting counts toward the 64-character limit.
dashboard.sablelife.description_damage_a: Output signals from cumulative actual HP loss or a timed damage requirement, with inversion and internal/external outputs.
dashboard.sablelife.accum_help:
Counts actual HP lost after part modifiers and adaptive defense. Reaching the threshold latches one pulse; excess damage and all hits during output are ignored. After the pulse ends, resets to zero and starts the next cycle. Internal channel: 0 disables, select an enabled Program internal / Program transmitter channel. Red/blue external output is independent and optional. Reverse On: normally high, interrupted for the pulse duration at threshold. Inactive modules output zero. Use a dedicated channel for stagger; other producers combine by maximum power.

Timed mode starts while triggered with a usable output and evaluates actual received HP damage only at the deadline. Invert Off outputs below the requirement; Invert On outputs at or above it, without an idle inverted high level. Once waits for trigger Off/On; Repeat starts a new window immediately after settlement. Early trigger Off cancels and clears without a failure pulse. Reset restarts while held On. Switching modes or timed criteria clears runtime, retaining hidden configuration. Internal channel, external red/blue frequency, strength and pulse remain shared and can output together.
manual.sablelife.damage_accumulation.set:
Cumulative mode counts the core's actual health loss after part modifiers and adaptive defense. Immune or zero-damage hits do not count, and healing does not subtract from the count. Threshold defaults to 100, accepts 1â€“1,000,000, and changes by 1 per wheel step.

Reaching the threshold schedules one pulse. Excess damage and hits during the pulse do not add to the next cycle. When the pulse ends, the count resets to zero. Pulse or interruption duration defaults to 1 second.

For internal output, select an enabled Sequence-controlled channel with internal output or external transmission; channel 0 leaves it unbound. For external Create output, choose red/blue frequency items. Internal and external output can operate separately or together.

Reverse Off normally outputs zero, then emits the configured strength when the threshold is reached. Reverse On normally emits that strength, then drops to zero for the pulse duration.

Timed mode measures actual health loss over a fixed window and checks the result only at the deadline. Invert Off outputs if the damage is below the requirement; Invert On outputs if it meets or exceeds the requirement. Timed Invert does not produce an idle high signal.

Once waits for the trigger to turn Off and On before starting another window. Repeat starts a new window after each check. Turning the trigger Off early cancels the window without a failure pulse. Reset starts it again if the trigger is still On. Changing the mode or timed criteria clears runtime progress but keeps the hidden settings.

Timed duration is 0.05â€“600 seconds, default 5. Required damage is 1â€“1,000,000, default 200. The requirement is total health lost, not DPS: 40 DPS over 5 seconds means a requirement of 200. Both modes use the same internal channel, external frequencies, strength and pulse settings.
manual.sablelife.damage_accumulation.exa:
1. Add Damage accumulation trigger, no mark needed.

2. Set threshold 100, channel 1, power 15 and duration 3 s. Enable Wireless channel 1 in Program internal mode.

3. Set Move set to Trigger: internal wireless, channel 1. Turn Reverse signal On on the accumulator.

4. Deal 30, 40 and 50 actual damage: one 3-second interruption begins; the extra 20 damage is discarded. Hits during that interruption do not count. After it ends, accumulation restarts at zero. When Move set loses its trigger, it cancels its current scheduling. After the signal returns it selects a move again; it does not resume the old timeline.

5. Assign red/blue frequency items if an external receiver is also needed.

Timed example: 5 seconds, 200 required damage, Invert Off. Less than 200 actual HP damage produces the punishment signal at the deadline; exactly 200 meets the requirement and produces no failure signal. Invert On outputs only on success.
manual.sablelife.damage_accumulation.tro:
In cumulative mode, losing the trigger, disabling the module or turning Master Off pauses a partial count or pending output. An already active pulse ends and resets its cycle. Outputs are zero while stopped. Re-enabling resumes an unfinished partial count or pending output.

Changing Threshold resets the count. Reset clears the count, pending output and active pulse. Death, Release and chunk unloading clear temporary progress. Copies and presets keep settings only.

Use a dedicated channel or frequency for an inverted interruption: another source holding that output high can hide the drop to zero. Healing cannot cancel the interruption. Incoming damage still reduces health during output; only counting is suspended.

This module can interrupt a Move set through its signal. It does not pose the structure, create a stagger animation or stop attacks already in flight.

Timed mode does not retain partial progress when its trigger stops. If the pulse lasts at least as long as the check window, consecutive matching windows can produce a continuous high signal.
dashboard.sablelife.description_signal_t: Turns the connected Sable structure using six analog wireless inputs. A marked face defines its front.
dashboard.sablelife.signal_turn_help: Mark a front face. Each direction selects an internal-output or external-receiver channel; 0 disables that direction. Each axis speed scales linearly with strength / 15. Opposite strengths subtract: 120 deg/s at strength 7 gives 56 deg/s. Active signal turning takes priority over Auto facing; Teleport takes priority over both; continuous Travel can steer while moving. Collision On uses the existing safe body bounds, can limit large-machine rotation and allows clear axes to continue when another is blocked. Off forces rotation at the configured analog speed.
dashboard.sablelife.turn_state_partial: Blocked axis skipped; other axes turning
color_picker.sablelife.title: Color: %s
color_picker.sablelife.help: Square: saturation and brightness. Strip: hue. Original color on the left, selected color on the right. Numeric edits move the picker; drag moves the numeric values.
manual.sablelife.signal_turn.settings:
Mark a face that points toward the structure's front. Each direction has its own channel and input source: internal wireless output or external wireless receive. The six inputs are Left, Right, Up, Down, clockwise roll and counterclockwise roll. Channel 0 disables that direction.

Internal inputs need an enabled waveform/program output. External inputs need an enabled receiver. Per-axis speed at strength 15 accepts 0â€“720 degrees per second, defaults to 120, and changes by 5 per wheel step.

Actual speed is configured speed Ã— input strength / 15. With speed 120, strength 15 gives 120 degrees per second, strength 7 gives 56, and 0 stops.

Opposite inputs subtract on the same axis. Left 15 and Right 7 therefore give a net left turn of 64 degrees per second. Several axes can turn together, so combined rotation can be faster than the rate of one axis alone.
manual.sablelife.signal_turn.example:
1. Add Signal turning and mark the machine front.

2. Set speed 120 and left input to internal channel 1. Enable channel 1 in Program internal mode.

3. Supply strength 7 to channel 1 to turn left at nominal 56 degrees/s; 15 gives 120.

4. Bind right to channel 2. Equal left/right strengths stop yaw; a stronger right signal turns right.

5. Configure up/down and roll only if needed, or use external receiver channels for your redstone control system.
manual.sablelife.signal_turn.troubleshoo:
Signal turning does not select or track targets. No net signal allows Auto facing to run if separately active. With net input, the first available Signal turning module controls rotation and pauses Auto facing, including when rotation is blocked. Teleport has priority; continuous Travel can steer while moving.

Collision defaults On, using contact-deflated body bounds and the existing safe rotation sweep. Large machines may be limited below nominal speed; blocked axes are skipped while clear axes continue. Off ignores those blockers. Death, disable, invalid/lost marks and master Off stop module rotation. Keep front markers, channel modes and opposing signal strengths consistent.
manual.sablelife.module_management.color:
Color picker

For settings that support color, click RGB to choose hue, saturation and brightness visually. Expand Precise RGB to enter values from 0 to 255. The preview compares the original and new colors. Confirm saves the choice; Cancel or Esc discards it. Use presets returns to preset colors while keeping the custom value for later.
manual.sablelife.module_management.manua:
Language and layout

Language switches between English and Simplified Chinese without restarting. Density adjusts the layout to your window and GUI scale. The manual keeps your chapter, tab and search when returning; right-click the density button to cycle backward.
manual.sablelife.server_limits.usage: Server limits prevent unusually large configurations from using unbounded resources. They do not change ordinary attack damage, part damage modifiers or action timing. In multiplayer, administrators configure these limits on the server.
manual.sablelife.server_limits.settings:
The world's serverconfig/sablelife-server.toml contains the resource limits. Defaults include 256 newly configured wireless channels, 8,192 particle points per player per tick, 8,192 loaded Sable Life projectiles per dimension, 2,048 per creature, 256 cleanup blocks per server tick, and 8,388,608 collision checks per dimension per tick.

Existing saved channels keep their numbers. New-projectile limits do not delete saved projectiles or ones already in flight.

When the collision budget is exhausted, movement waits and reports that state. Terrain can still block it normally. The particle budget may reduce decorative output. Death cleanup shares its budget across pending jobs; unloaded blocks remain protected until they can be cleaned up.

maximumModulesPerCreature limits newly added modules to 128 by default and can be set from 16 to 256. Existing saved modules are retained up to 256. Add follows the server's limit, and Hit counter can select sources across the expanded module list.

Entity hitboxes default to 8 per creature (maximumEntityHitboxesPerCreature, 1â€“32). Blueprint model projection defaults to 8,192 blocks; larger or unsupported multipart projections use bounds only. Natural-spawn limits are separate from Arena limits.

Module switches are grouped by [modules.heartCore], [modules.redstoneCore] and [modules.survivalHeartCore]. Survival material prices and multipliers are under [survivalTokens]. Use the server's loaded sablelife-server.toml; client changes do not set multiplayer prices or limits.

allowEditHeartCoreUnderSurvivalMode defaults to false. Enabling it permits ordinary Heart Core editing in Survival mode, including loot, experience rewards and terrain destruction. It is separate from the Survival Heart Core, which does not need this switch.
manual.sablelife.server_limits.example: Before raising a limit, test a modest structure with the actual mods and player count you expect to use. Watch server tick time and network traffic to nearby players. The configured limits do not guarantee a particular TPS or number of creatures.
manual.sablelife.server_limits.troublesh:
Only administrators can create or approve command modules. Blueprint placement has no player identity, so imported commands need administrator approval in the command editor before they can run. Importing a normal module preset does not grant command permissions.

Editing requests and complex imports are rate-limited. If a rapid series of requests is rejected, pause briefly before trying again.
core.sablelife.deathEffectRadius_help: Lethal-hit effects use the center of the connected body. 0 automatically fits its enclosing sphere; a positive value specifies a radius up to 256 blocks. Spread adds jitter. Flash stays at the center. Delayed removal effects remain on individual blocks.
manual.sablelife.core.death_envelope:
Death effect shape
The immediate effect surrounds the connected structure, including limbs. Radius 0 fits it automatically, up to 256 blocks; a positive radius fixes the size. Spread varies positions. Burst/cloud start around the sphere; ring/star/spiral keep their shapes; Flash stays central. Sound range is separate.

Vanish effects appear at blocks being removed after Death delay, including batched cleanup. Reward positions do not move.
manual.sablelife.core.protected_tools:
Player mining has three modes: Prohibited, Always allowed, and Only after death. The mining-drops switch controls allowed player-mined block items separately. Explosion destruction is a separate rule; enabling mining drops does not make explosions drop blocks.

An active ordinary Heart Core itself remains protected from Survival mining even if its body is mineable. Detached parts keep the creature's applicable protection until release or cleanup. Default detached-part cleanup is 3 seconds; it is configured separately from limb loot.

When mining is prohibited, supported tool hits damage the active creature instead of mining its blocks. Ordinary terrain keeps its normal mining behavior.
core.sablelife.bossbar_color_help: Boss bar color: click forward, right-click backward. Uses the seven vanilla colors.
manual.sablelife.core.boss_colors:
Boss bar color
Use the selector beside Boss bar. Left/right click cycles forward/backward; Red is the default. Color is saved and may change while alive without resetting health.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.cleanup: Cleanup progress is saved with the world. If you leave during a large creatureâ€™s batched removal, loading the world again resumes the remaining cleanup instead of restarting the whole death or granting its reward again. Unloaded areas wait until loaded; this is different from the death-delay countdown. Removal effects remain at the blocks being cleaned.
manual.sablelife.melee.epic_guard:
With supported Epic Fight 21.17.3.1, Melee module attacks can be guarded or parried using its normal front-facing, held-weapon and skill rules. Native stamina, penalty, guard-break animation and parry timing remain in effect. The attack origin is the marked bodyâ€™s world position; attacks from behind are not blocked.

A blocked contact waits for the configured Interval before trying again, without applying damage, hit effects or module knockback. Successful-hit limits are not consumed by blocks. No proxy attacker is spawned. This bridge does not change Arrow/Gun blocking or make all module attacks blockable.
arena_buffs.sablelife.title: Arena buff groups
arena_buffs.sablelife.help: All groups share Nearby player range around the living core, using horizontal distance. Alive survival players only. The Arena must be enabled, marked and triggered, with Range buffs On. Follow module needs no extra signal; internal reads the selected channel output, external reads its input. Channel 0 is unbound. Groups may overlap; strongest level wins for the same effect. Refreshes once per second for 2 seconds, then expires naturally. Existing stronger/longer potion effects are not removed. Instant effects are unavailable. Up to 16 groups / 16 effects each. Presets keep effects but require rebinding channels.
manual.sablelife.arena.range_buffs:
Range buffs
Defaults Off. Up to 16 groups, each with 16 persistent effects at levels 1-5; no instant healing/damage. Effects last 2 seconds and refresh once per second.

Only living Survival players in the same dimension and within horizontal Player range around the core receive them, even while the creature is inside its arena. The module must be enabled, marked and triggered.

Follow module needs no extra input. Internal/External channel reads a core output/receiver; 0 is unbound. External frequencies are set in Wireless. Highest level wins when groups overlap.

For a phase change, send Health phase outputs to separate channels and bind the groups. Signal loss, leaving range, disabling or death stops refresh; effects expire naturally, may briefly overlap and do not clear unrelated effects. Config copies retain bindings; presets need new channel bindings.
manual.sablelife.core.iron_spells:
Ironâ€™s Spells compatibility targets the inspected Minecraft 1.21.1 / 3.16.3 release. Supported moving damage projectiles are Magic missile, Magic arrow, Small fireball, Firebolt, Icicle, Lightning lance and Blood slash, plus Fireball and Fire arrow explosions. Hitting a living body consumes the projectile, including piercing types, after one body damage calculation. Ordinary living targets keep native behavior. Explosive projectiles retain native blast damage and effects without a second TNT-formula hit.

Fire breath, Cone of cold and Poison breath use their native attack-part boxes and damage activation windows. Multiple parts touching one creature count once per window. Terrain blocks these attacks. Ray of siphoning uses the native ray and cast pulses; it heals the caster by actual body health removed. Blood slash retains its native 15% lifesteal. Part modifiers and adaptive defense still apply; fully immune bodies do not provide healing.

No proxy entities are spawned. Unknown projectile families, lock-on, chains, lightning balls and other ground waves still need explicit adapters. Burning, freezing, poison status effects and native LivingEntity-only damage/skill events are not simulated on bodies. Addons retaining a supported path can inherit it; independent paths need verification. Unverified Iron versions receive no hooks.
manual.sablelife.core.iron_areas:
Additional inspected paths: Shadow slash damages real body voxels in its impact area. Wither skull applies one full direct body hit and nearby damage; Starfall comets apply their native flat area damage; Arrow volleyâ€™s individual small arrows each damage once and stop at a body. Sunbeam retains its native 15-tick warmup and single area burst.

Earthquake, Fire fields and Poison clouds follow the native checkHits cadence, startup delay and duration. Circular areas retain the radius as well as their vertical box limits. One pulse can hit several creatures, but multiple body blocks count once per creature; hit-based radius and duration changes occur once for the entire pulse. An immune contact still counts for these native post-hit rules.

Healing areas and freeze-only fields are not converted into body damage, even when their internal amount is positive. Body damage does not simulate native poison, fire or freezing status ticks. Other area families still need verification.
arena_respawn.sablelife.requires: Requires an interface-compatible Sable Photomancy and creative operator permission. See the server log if the API check fails.
arena_respawn.sablelife.failed: Respawn stopped. Use /sablelife_respawn cancel nearby to clear it.
arena_respawn.sablelife.missing: Respawn paused: Photomancy missing or API incompatible
arena_respawn.sablelife.error_unassemble: The core must belong to an assembled structure.
arena_respawn.sablelife.error_too_large: Template exceeds the structure or data limit.
arena_respawn.sablelife.error_unloaded: Load every connected part before recording.
arena_respawn.sablelife.error_one_heart: The template must contain exactly one heart core.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_respawn_help: Requires an interface-compatible Photomancy and a creative operator. Mark the arena center, record the current connected structure and enable automatic respawn. Cooldown begins at death; unloaded spawn chunks pause it. Old cleanup must finish before native one-call restoration. Large placements may cause a brief pause. The new creature activates at full health. Record again to replace the template; clear it to stop future respawns.
manual.sablelife.arena.respawn:
Record and enable
Automatic respawn defaults Off and needs compatible Sable Photomancy (tested 1.0.1). An interface failure disables respawn and identifies the missing member in the server log; other features remain usable.

As a Creative operator, mark Arena center, record the connected structure, enable respawn and set cooldown (default 60 seconds, minimum 5). Re-recording replaces that creature's record. The template retains relative poses, settings, modules, internal references and inventories; its basis anchor, not necessarily its bottom, goes to Arena center.

Respawn cycle
Cooldown starts at death. Placement waits for the old body/limbs to finish cleanup and for destination chunks to load; it does not force them. Native placement is synchronous and activates a fresh full-health creature with new IDs, rebound marks and reset runtime state. All rebuilt parts are registered even if joints are not ready. Incomplete restored parts pause their block-entity ticks until data/joints are applied, including after reload. The record is reused for later generations.

Countdown
Text/progress appears above a standable surface at the anchor X/Z, preferring below then above; without support it uses anchor height. This moves only the display. The countdown survives core deletion and world saves.

Stop or recover
Clear record stops future respawns, leaving the current creature. After core removal, an operator within 64 blocks of the anchor/display can use /sablelife_respawn cancel. It removes only that record's known partial bodies and orphan displays. Failed builds stop rather than duplicate; old incremental builds retain recovery support.

Limits and cautions
Records stay server-side, outside presets, client menu snapshots and ordinary blueprint copies. Limits: 32 records, 32 parts and 256 captured entities. Default configurable limits: 131,072 blocks, 16,384 block entities, 4,194,304 bounding-box cells, 32 MiB per template and 128 MiB per world. Rejections show actual/maximum amounts.

Unallocated plot gaps count as empty, without creating chunks. Nearby rope-adjacent builds need an actual connected-chain link to be captured. Supported joints/addon data are preserved; test other addons. Recorded inventories and rewards repeat intentionally. Large captures or native placement can pause the server.
manual.sablelife.core.iron_physical_foll:
Additional physical damage paths: Creeper mortar keeps its quadratic radius falloff; Divine smite uses its native forward box and weapon/spell damage; summoned fangs hit once at their native bite window on real ground; Ice block keeps its harmless floating phase, half-damage falling contact and cubic-falloff ground burst. A falling ice block consumed by body contact does not also burst on that same victim.

These adapters add no synthetic body entity, UUID target or entity lock-on. Native spells may retain their normal mob targeting, but the body damage paths use physical overlap, native ray positions or actual impact areas. Strict entity-targeted spells are excluded by scope. Pure freezing/poison/fire status effects still are not simulated on body voxels.
manual.sablelife.arena.respawn_notes:
Arena center places the blueprint's basis anchor, not its feet or lowest block. Large templates can extend below that anchor. Set the center high enough to clear the lowest parts and mounted equipment, and leave space around the whole structure. Ground-level placement does not automatically align its feet to the ground.

Overlapping terrain or other structures can push parts apart, launch the structure or strain joints. Moving Arena center after recording changes the respawn destination; it does not ground the template automatically.

The countdown is positioned independently near terrain, so a high spawn anchor does not force the text into the sky. Test a full death and respawn cycle before using the encounter.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.did_you:
One creature can run only one Linear movement at a time, including charging. If two modules become ready together, the earlier one in the module list starts. Their speeds and directions do not add together.

The other can start later only if its trigger is still active and its own cooldown allows it. A short signal may end before that happens. An earlier module with a continuous trigger can keep taking precedence. This also applies when different Move sets request movement.
manual.sablelife.move_set.did_you_know:
Within one Move set, eligible Priority moves are checked in move-list order. The first available one is selected, rather than chosen randomly. If it is unavailable or cooling down, the next eligible Priority move can run.

Priority does not interrupt a move already running. Selection happens when the controller is ready for its next move. Weighted selection is used only when no Priority move is eligible.

Separate Move sets select independently and can run together. Referencing the same action module from both does not create a second runtime instance.
manual.sablelife.core.whole_cleanup:
Cleanup
After Death delay, a fully loaded creature can be removed in one tick if every non-air block belongs to its cleanup group. Unloaded parts wait; mixed ownership or failed checks use batched cleanup. Supported mounted cannons/bearing contraptions and attached decorations are cleaned with their registered controllers, without affecting unrelated controllers.

At most one whole-creature deletion is attempted per tick, with up to 1,048,576 registered coordinates. Larger groups use batches. A large atomic deletion can still pause the server; the per-block budget does not split it.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_record_release: Keep the recorded structure up to date.
dashboard.sablelife.runtime_trigger_soun: Signal active: listening for contact; ordinary trigger audio follows its mode
sound_timeline.sablelife.fade_help: Fade out during the final seconds within the limit; a fade longer than the limit uses the entire interval. 0 cuts off immediately. A zero limit disables fading. Does not extend a sound that ends naturally sooner.
core.sablelife.survivalInteraction_help: Off by default. Off blocks survival/adventure right-click use of living body devices and frequency changes; creative players may operate them. On allows device use; placement and breaking retain their own rules.
dashboard.sablelife.sensor_output_help: Detection radius is 1â€“64 blocks, default 12. A detected target supplies 15 weak redstone power into the Mark block through the selected face, so a marked redstone lamp lights up. Mark receives power; it does not emit power from all faces. Internal channel and external red/blue frequencies are simultaneous outputs. Internal 0 is unbound; enable Module output mode in the core Wireless page. Channel strength does not change Markâ€™s 15 power. Additional outputs follow Wireless master; a Redstone Core also stops detection when master is off. Invert applies to Mark and channel outputs: no target powers them, a target turns them off. Inversion requires an active triggered module; disable/death clears output.
wireless.sablelife.name: Name
wireless.sablelife.name_help: Name this channel (up to 40 characters). Apply with Enter or âœ“. The sidebar keeps the channel number and signal state before its name. Empty clears the name; names do not change signal timing or frequency.
dashboard.sablelife.description_gyroscop: Records a preferred posture and brings the connected Sable structure back toward it when it tilts too far.
dashboard.sablelife.gyro_collision_note: Avoids obstacles while righting; Off may turn into terrain
dashboard.sablelife.gyro_preview_help: Cyan: world down. Orange: calibrated body-down direction. Green: allowed tilt cone.
dashboard.sablelife.gyro_help: Mark a reference part, pose the assembled machine as desired, then record its current posture as level. The chosen face need not point down. Calibration stores a local direction and survives Release, reactivation and world reload. Beyond the tilt limit it smoothly rights the connected parts; yaw is not locked. Fully level keeps recovering to level; Inside limit stops 3Â° within the boundary. Linear movement takes priority; recovery pauses Signal turning and Auto facing. Collision checks default On; Off ignores colliders but still requires loaded valid destinations. Re-marking or transferring the reference to a new part requires recalibration; portable presets/configuration copies also require it. Choose the main torso or a fixed reference part rather than a moving joint. It does not lift or hover; collision-safe turns on large machines may be slower than the configured rate. Hover anchor can hold position while Gyroscope rights the body around its marked point; enabling Lock rotation pauses Gyroscope.
manual.sablelife.gyroscope.settings:
Calibration records the world-down direction in the marked part's local axes. This lets a sloped part define the structure's preferred posture. Use a fixed main-body part rather than a moving joint.

Maximum tilt accepts 0â€“180 degrees and defaults to 20. Righting speed accepts 0.1â€“720 degrees per second and defaults to 90. Fully level restores the calibrated posture. Inside limit stops 3 degrees inside the tilt threshold. Rotation collision checking defaults On.

Correction keeps translation and spin around the world's vertical axis; it is not a heading lock. It provides no lift or hovering. Collision-safe correction on a large structure can be slower than the configured speed.

Hover anchor can hold position while Gyroscope corrects tilt around the anchor point. If the anchor's Lock rotation is On, Gyroscope waits.

Maximum tilt is the start threshold in both recovery modes; Righting speed controls both modes. Fully level continues to the calibrated level posture, while Back inside tilt limit stops inside the allowed tilt.
manual.sablelife.gyroscope.example:
1. Add Gyroscope and mark a fixed reference part.

2. While the creature is dormant, position the assembled Sable structure in the posture you want.

3. Click Record current posture as level.

4. Set the tilt limit and righting speed, then Preview and activate. Release and world reload keep this calibration.
manual.sablelife.gyroscope.troubleshooti:
Gyroscope waits while Teleport or non-gravity Linear movement controls the complete pose. It can correct tilt during gravity-affected Travel.

The first recovering Gyroscope takes rotation priority even if blocked, pausing Signal turning and Auto facing. When no correction is needed, those controllers can run.

Collision, an exhausted work budget or an unloaded destination pauses correction without loading chunks. Losing the reference mark, disabling the module, losing its trigger, death or Wireless Master Off stops it.

Re-marking onto a different reference body or an assembly transfer can clear calibration. Generic presets and configuration clipboard copies require a fresh mark and calibration. Native copies of the complete structure retain the module data. Test large articulated machines with their actual motors and joints.
armor_rules.sablelife.title: Phase damage rules
armor_rules.sablelife.help: Each row applies while powered or unpowered. Unpowered mode applies until a signal arrives, pauses while powered and resumes when it ends. Unbound channels do not apply. Lowest matching modifier wins.
phase_rules.sablelife.title: Health phase rules
phase_rules.sablelife.help: Rows run independently while lower < HP% <= upper. Hold stays on in range; Enter pulses once on entry. Leaving range or losing the outer trigger cancels it. Overlaps can output together; the highest strength wins on a shared channel. Choose an enabled, configured Sequence output channel.
loot_editor.sablelife.mode_help: Chance checks each slot independently. Weighted mode draws from positive weights for the configured number of draws.
loot_editor.sablelife.edit_help: Edit quantity and chance/weight using inputs, buttons or the wheel. Shift-left raises the rule; Shift-right lowers it.
loot_editor.sablelife.template_help: Left selects; with an item, left copies the stack and right adds one. Empty-handed right removes one. Shift-left/right adjusts chance or weight. Shift-click inventory copies into the first empty sample. No items are consumed.
dashboard.sablelife.pulse_visual_help: Fixed boundary ring preserves the original style. Outward sphere expands from the release center to Radius over 0.05â€“10 seconds, default 0.5 seconds. Cosmetic only: damage and knockback still resolve immediately, with no extra hits during expansion. Center and wave/boundary particles can be selected separately, with size and lifetime. Empty a group to disable it. Outward particle lifetime is at least the expansion time so it reaches the boundary.
dashboard.sablelife.redstone_channel_hel: Outputs to this core's Wireless channel; 0 disables it. Enable the channel and select Sequence / internal. Uses strength, Hold/Pulse and inversion. No Mark or frequency items required; all three destinations can work together. Highest strength wins across producers. Use different input/output channels to avoid self-latching.
dashboard.sablelife.pullStrength_note: Inward speed gain per tick; higher pulls up to speed faster
dashboard.sablelife.pullSpeed_note: Caps inward speed; sideways movement is preserved
dashboard.sablelife.description_hover_an: Pin the marked block at its current position while allowing the body to swing freely.
dashboard.sablelife.hover_help: XYZ use world axes; only enabled axes are pinned. Hard pin has no offset. Elastic pin returns within the maximum offset on each enabled axis. Damping reduces elastic movement and free rotation; 0 preserves natural swinging. Enable XYZ and Lock rotation to fix the marked partâ€™s position and posture.
manual.sablelife.hover_anchor.settings:
Choose which world axes to pin: X, Y and Z. Hard pin allows no offset on enabled axes. Elastic pin lets the point move within a per-axis limit, then pulls it back. Damping reduces elastic movement and free rotation; 0 preserves natural swinging.

Enable all three axes and Lock rotation to hold the marked part's position and posture. Rotation lock applies to that part; connected bearing-driven parts can still move.
manual.sablelife.hover_anchor.example:
1. Mark a block on the intended part. Defaults pin X, Y and Z firmly, allow free rotation, and use damping 0.

2. Enable only Y to hold height while allowing horizontal movement. Enable only X and Z to allow vertical movement.

3. For an elastic suspension, choose Elastic pin. Start with strength 20 and a 2-block limit on each enabled axis, then tune the damping.

4. With all axes and Lock rotation Off, and damping 0, the module creates no constraint.
manual.sablelife.hover_anchor.troublesho:
Activation records the current world position and posture, so no calibration is needed. Turning it Off, death, mark loss or unloading releases the joint. Reload captures a new position when it activates again.

The first triggered anchor takes priority over Linear movement, Signal turning and Auto facing. With free rotation, Gyroscope can correct tilt around the marked point while the anchor holds position. Lock rotation instead gives the anchor control of posture and pauses Gyroscope.

Elastic limits apply to each enabled axis, not to a spherical radius. Rotation lock fixes the marked part; bearing-connected parts may still move under their own drives. Tune elasticity and damping for the actual structure, especially on large articulated builds.
dashboard.sablelife.hover_note: Mark a pivot on the structure. Activation pins its current position while leaving rotation free. Off releases it. No world calibration needed.
dashboard.sablelife.description_hit_coun: Count successful HP-damaging module hits and output an internal pulse at the threshold.
dashboard.sablelife.description_health_a: Heals or drains this creature on activation, or repeatedly while its trigger stays active.
dashboard.sablelife.hit_counter_help:
Count only actual HP loss; blocked, invulnerable, zero-damage or absorption-only hits do not count. Select a source by its sidebar number; its stable ID is retained. Interval 0 counts every damage application. Use a larger interval for continuous attacks. Output needs an enabled Sequence / internal channel. Counting pauses during the pulse, then resets; trigger Off clears the count.
Optional external red/blue frequencies can output without an internal channel. If both outputs are configured, they share the same count, strength and pulse duration.
dashboard.sablelife.health_adjustment_he: Positive heals; negative drains. Percent uses maximum HP. Once executes on a rising edge, or once per Move Set action window. Periodic executes immediately and repeats at the interval. Drain bypasses defenses without incoming-hit effects or hit credit; by default it leaves at least 1 HP. Lethal drain follows normal death/respawn. Healing is capped at maximum HP and cannot revive a dead life.
manual.sablelife.hit_counter.settings:
The counter counts actual health-damaging hits from a selected Sable Life module. Blocked, immune, zero-damage and absorption-only hits do not count. Select the source by its sidebar number; the reference stores its stable ID, so reordering modules does not change the source.

Interval 0 counts every damage application. Increase it to limit counting from continuous attacks. The interval is shared across targets. Reaching the threshold emits a pulse; counting pauses during the pulse and then resets. Turning the trigger Off clears the count.

Internal output needs an enabled Sequence-controlled channel in Internal output mode. Red/blue frequency items provide an optional external output, which can also work on its own. If both are configured, they use the same count, strength and pulse. Stopping the core or disabling/removing the module clears transmission.
manual.sablelife.health_adjustment.setti:
Positive values heal the creature; negative values drain its health. Percent uses maximum health as the basis.

Once runs on a rising trigger, or once for each Move set action window. Periodic runs immediately and then repeats at its Interval.

Drain bypasses defense and produces no incoming-hit effects or hit credit. By default, it leaves at least 1 HP. Enable lethal drain to allow normal death and respawn behavior. Healing cannot exceed maximum health or revive a dead creature.
manual.sablelife.hit_counter.example:
1. Add Hit counter, select an attack source, set Threshold to 5 and internal output to channel 3.

2. In Wireless, enable channel 3 as Sequence-controlled with Internal output.

3. Add Health adjustment with an Internal wireless trigger on channel 3. Set Once and +10 HP.

4. Deal five successful health-damaging hits with the selected attack. The counter pulses and the creature heals 10 HP.
manual.sablelife.hit_counter.troubleshoo:
Supported sources include this mod's Melee, Flamethrower, Arrow launcher, Gun, Mortar, Hovering homing salvo, Laser beam, Sphere blast, Slash, Ground strike, Earthquake wave and Shockwave, including hits on mechanical creatures. External weapons such as CBC mounts do not have a Sable Life module identity and do not count.

Area hits count per target, subject to the counter's shared minimum interval. A projectile's direct hit and explosion count separately if each removes health. Later potion or burning status damage does not count.

Counts are not saved; reload starts at zero. Generic presets require both the source and output to be selected again.
manual.sablelife.health_adjustment.examp:
For an attack cost, add a negative Once adjustment to a Move set. For phase regeneration, use a positive Periodic adjustment triggered by a held internal channel.

Defaults are +10 HP, Once, Fixed HP, a 1-second interval and lethal drain Off.
manual.sablelife.health_adjustment.troub:
This is a core module and needs no mark. It is unavailable on Redstone Cores.

Always with Once runs only once after activation; choose Periodic for repeated healing. Multiple Health adjustment modules run independently in module-list order. Reactivation or reload resets their clocks.
dashboard.sablelife.description_visual_s: Creates mechanical patterns, symbols, screen distortion, shake, zoom or color effects.
dashboard.sablelife.shock_help: Mark the origin and facing; Preview plays once. World patterns can follow the part or keep their release pose. Symbols face the camera. Contact mode plays at the contact point.
manual.sablelife.visual_shockwave.settin:
Spatial effect
Ring shockwave is the default. Radial blur stretches the world outward from the actual emission point's screen position, leaving a clear center; adjust strength, duration and clear-center radius (% of screen height). Released effects stay at their release position. Behind-camera sources draw no ring/blur; HUD stays sharp.

Reverse contracts a ring from Radius to center over Expansion time. It does not reverse shake, zoom or distance fading.

Camera
Spatial effect, Shake and Zoom have separate switches, default On; 0 strength omits a component. Shake works behind the viewer. Frequency (default 1x, 0.1-2x) changes oscillation speed. Positive zoom moves in, negative out; distance fades effects, and the client Distortion Effects setting scales them (0 disables).

Repeat without contact holds zoom while triggered; Interval only spaces waves. Signal end, disabling/removal, Master Off or cleanup releases it. Once/contact/Preview zoom is temporary.

Color filter
Default Off; choose preset/RGB, strength and fade times. All players within Effect range receive the same strength. The filter follows the trigger independently of Once/Repeat/contact; exit or signal loss fades out, re-entry blends from its current color. Waves do not restart its fade. Death/Release/Master Off/disable/delete stops it. Filters blend; the client setting scales them too. Preview holds about 3 seconds before fading.
manual.sablelife.visual_shockwave.exampl:
1. For a roar, add Visual Effects and mark a mouth block. Defaults are radius 18, expansion 0.45 seconds, width 1.5, distortion 0.35, blur 0.25, shake 0.15 for 0.4 seconds, zoom-in 4% with 0.5-second recovery, and effect range 64.

2. Use Preview to see the configured result without damage or movement. Schedule it with the roar sound in a Move set, or use an internal channel.

3. For footsteps, enable Block contact trigger. Mark the foot, choose Down, distance 0.25 and cooldown 0.3 seconds. Keep the module enabled with Always or a Move set action. Set distortion, blur and zoom to 0 for shake only. The probe follows the marked part and ignores its own creature.

4. For a purple phase effect, turn Spatial wave, Camera shake and Camera zoom Off. Enable Color filter, choose purple, strength 0.25, fade-in 0.2 seconds and fade-out 0.4 seconds. A Move set action or internal signal controls how long it lasts.

Radial roar: enable Spatial effect, choose Radial blur, strength 0.35, duration 0.6 seconds and clear-center radius 8%. Mark the mouth/emitter. Combine with shake and a roar sound; use Preview to tune it. The blur has no damage or collision.
manual.sablelife.visual_shockwave.troubl:
A released wave stays at its world position instead of following the moving mouth or limb. Turning the camera changes its screen projection. The ring does not test spherical depth against walls, so walls do not hide it.

Camera effects change the rendered view and field of view, not attack aim or structure collision. Once uses a rising signal or Move set action window; Repeat emits at its interval. Released waves finish naturally and are cleared when leaving the world.

The client keeps the newest 8 events and can render all 8 visible rings. Combined camera effects are capped. A rendering failure safely disables distortion. Third-party shaders, HDR and alternate framebuffers may omit rings and need testing.
wireless.sablelife.latch_help: Latch holds the first nonzero output strength after its pulse ends. Reset reads this core's internal output, or external input on a receiving channel. Reset wins; the original input must go low before it can set again. Receive mode does not latch. Disabling, master off, configuration edits, death, release or reload clear runtime state; settings remain.
core.sablelife.killHeal_help: Off by default. Instantly restores this living core to maximum HP when its own attack confirms a survival/adventure player kill. Hits, mob kills, totems, canceled deaths and unrelated deaths do not count. Dead cores are not revived. Supports direct module attacks and owned projectiles; later environmental or damage-over-time deaths are not inferred.
dashboard.sablelife.melee_expand_help: Adds to the two-Mark box. Length extends forward from the first Mark face; width and height expand equally on both sides. Angles rotate the extended box. Start distance moves the whole box. Preview shows the final hitbox.
moveset.sablelife.problem_missing: Referenced module was deleted or is missing
moveset.sablelife.problem_unsupported: This module type cannot be used as a move action
dashboard.sablelife.shot_aim_help: Target mode aims at current visible target positions when firing. Off: nearest target; Multiple target on: one full burst/fan per target, up to 64. Search range is separate from projectile travel range. No target means no release. Flights do not track or predict motion; arrows retain gravity. Slash offset angles still apply.
dashboard.sablelife.move_gravity_help: Travel: Step assist is independent of Affected by gravity and always available. Any grounded part meeting a low obstacle raises the whole connected machine together over 6 ticks. Gravity on retains falling/rotation; gravity off retains the raised route height until this movement finishes. One shared cooldown; continuous obstruction cannot repeatedly step. No headroom prediction. Hover Anchor takes precedence. Vertical aiming and Force movement are ignored only when gravity is on.
dashboard.sablelife.move_gravity_preview: Horizontal route only: physics determines falling, tilt and step clearance.
dashboard.sablelife.move_step_preview: Base route preview only. Obstacle-triggered whole-machine steps are added during movement; collision clearance may differ.
dashboard.sablelife.description_distorti: Leaves a narrowing, fading ribbon of refraction when the marked blade or part moves. This effect causes no damage.
dashboard.sablelife.distortion_trail_hel: One Mark; its face points along the blade from root to tip. Length spans the blade; width/height set ribbon thickness. Moving or rotating above threshold connects adjacent poses into a continuous refractive ribbon. Older trail narrows and fades; stationary marks emit nothing. Spacing controls curve subdivision, with both endpoints retained every moving tick (up to 8 samples). Separate strokes and teleports over 64 blocks never bridge. Preview outlines the marked volume. Supports Move set and control cores. Screen effects Off hides it. Screen projection can affect foreground surfaces; this is visual refraction, not damage or smoke. Hurt Once detects movement for one lifetime window. Bounded to 128 samples/module and 256/client; longer dense paths can discard the oldest tail.
manual.sablelife.distortion_trail.settin:
Mark one block face pointing along the blade from root to tip. Length spans the blade; Width and Height set the trail's thickness.

Movement or rotation above the threshold joins successive poses into a continuous ribbon of refraction. Older sections narrow and fade. A stationary mark emits nothing. Spacing controls curve subdivision, keeping both endpoints each moving tick with up to 8 samples. Separate strokes and teleports over 64 blocks are not joined.

Preview outlines the marked volume. The module can be scheduled by Move set. Administrators can also allow it on Redstone Cores, where it is enabled by default. Hurt Once watches movement for one trail-lifetime window.

This is screen-space refraction, not smoke or damage, and it can affect foreground surfaces in the view. Turning screen effects Off hides it. Limits are 128 samples per module and 256 per client; dense or long paths may lose their oldest sections.
manual.sablelife.distortion_trail.exampl:
1. Mark a sword or tail part. Point the marked face along its length.

2. Try Length 6, Width and Height 1.5, lifetime 0.5 seconds, strength 0.35 and spacing 0.35.

3. Use a Move set action to enable the trail during a swing, or Always to let movement detection decide when it appears.

4. Move the part and inspect the ribbon from a visible camera angle.
manual.sablelife.distortion_trail.troubl:
The module needs a valid mark and active trigger. Its first activation records a starting pose; movement after that creates the trail.

Movement below the threshold, strength 0, being out of range, screen effects Off, or a source behind the camera can hide it. Pure rotation uses an estimate of the blade edge's speed.

Visual budgets can thin the ribbon without changing collision or attacks. Death, mark loss, disabling or reload clears tracking. Existing visuals expire within 3 seconds. Test large articulated structures and shader combinations in game.
dashboard.sablelife.module_search_help: Search names, module types or numbers across all pages. #12 matches the original number exactly. Clear to show all.
dashboard.sablelife.copy_module_help: Duplicate the selected module immediately after it, retaining Marks, settings and references with a new module identity.
dashboard.sablelife.description_surface_: An impact-only area damage template referenced by attacks. Configure radius or length/width/angle, duration, damage interval, particles, effects and residual burning. It has no Mark, target-position release or independent trigger.
dashboard.sablelife.field_help: Impact-only template: select this module in an attackâ€™s Area damage on impact. Homing projectiles also support it. Repeated hits from the same attack/template at the same surface patch refresh duration without stacking damage or restarting the hit clock. Radius/length/width wheel steps are 1 block, duration is 1 second. No Mark or independent target release.
manual.sablelife.surface_field.usage:
Persistent area damage is a template used by attacks when they hit. Create the template, then select it in Area damage on impact on Mortar, Flamethrower, Gun, Arrow, Slash, Laser, Ground strike or Hovering homing salvo.

The template does not run by itself. It has no mark, preview or independent trigger, and cannot be scheduled directly as a Move set action. Its activation is fixed to On impact. Its target filter chooses who can be damaged inside the area, not where the area appears.
manual.sablelife.surface_field.settings:
Circle uses a radius. Rectangle uses length, width, angle and centered or forward placement. Radius, length and width change by 1 block per wheel step; area duration changes by 1 second.

At 0 degrees, the area follows the incoming direction projected onto the impact surface. At 90 degrees, it runs across that direction. A perpendicular hit uses a stable direction on the surface.

Area damage has its own hit interval and ignores normal hurt immunity, including immunity from recent burning hits. Ignite on contact refreshes burning on each contact tick; once a target leaves, the remaining burn time counts down. Choose particles, Color/Life/Size and potion effects separately.

Particle density sets the number of visual sample points per particle type every 0.2 seconds. It accepts 0â€“128 and defaults to 24. A value of 0 hides particles without disabling damage, burning or effects. Small surfaces and the shared particle budget can reduce the actual count. Changes apply to newly created areas.
manual.sablelife.surface_field.example:
1. Add a Persistent area damage template and name it Poison field.

2. Set radius 4, duration 8 seconds, damage 3 and a hit interval of 1 second. Choose green effect particles.

3. In Hovering homing salvo, select Poison field under Area damage on impact. Trigger the salvo and let a projectile hit a surface.

4. Further hits from the same source and template near that patch refresh its 8-second lifetime. They do not stack another field or cause an immediate extra hit.

5. For a fire strip instead, use a rectangle with length 8, width 2 and angle 90 degrees. Select flame particles and configure 3 seconds of residual burning.
manual.sablelife.surface_field.troublesh:
Flames here are particles and burning effects, not real fire blocks. A moving Sable structure hit places the area on supporting ground rather than attaching a floating field to the structure. Areas can follow static ground steps within 2 blocks or the hit wall surface; unsupported air and moving structures are not painted.

Nearby impacts from the same attack source and template refresh the existing patch. Overlapping patches from that source and template share a per-target damage interval. Different attack sources remain independent. Each creature can have up to 64 active areas.

Death, unloading, global wireless stop, or disabling/deleting the source or template clears its areas. Active areas are not saved. In-flight attacks stop creating them if their source or template becomes unavailable.
