Saved projectiles keep the selected template reference. An embedded arrow does not create another area after reload. An explosive block hit creates it once before the arrow is discarded. Portable presets clear module references, so select the template again after importing.

Older Mark or On target release settings are ignored. If an old Move set scheduled this template directly, schedule the emitting attack instead and select the template on that attack. Only actual impacts create areas; a template does not need a valid old mark.
dashboard.sablelife.description_signal_l: Combine internal channel conditions and output one hold signal or rising-edge pulse. No Mark needed.
dashboard.sablelife.description_combat_e: Emit a channel pulse after the configured number of attributed kills or blocked attacks.
signal_rules.sablelife.title: Signal rules
signal_rules.sablelife.logic_help: All enabled inputs must reference configured channels. Unbound/missing inputs never satisfy NOT. Output uses a sequence/internal channel.
signal_rules.sablelife.event_help: Count attributed kills or blocked attacks. Events required: 1â€“9999, default 1. At the threshold, emit once and reset for the next cycle. Cooldown starts at output; events during cooldown do not count. Disabling or editing a rule clears its progress.
manual.sablelife.signal_logic.settings:
Add up to 16 input rows and enable the ones you want to use. Each row selects an internal channel, numbered from 1, and checks Powered or Unpowered. Choose All for AND or Any for OR, then set the output channel, strength and Hold or rising-edge Pulse mode.

An empty input list or an invalid enabled input prevents output, including for Unpowered checks. The output channel cannot also be an input. Configure the output channel as Sequence-controlled internal output.

All Signal logic modules read their inputs before any of them updates its output. A chain therefore advances one link per server tick, or 0.05 seconds, regardless of module order. Feedback is not evaluated recursively within one tick.

A pulse completes its duration even if the input condition stops matching. Losing the module trigger or disabling/removing the module stops output. The module does not automatically latch its result.
manual.sablelife.signal_logic.example:
1. Use channel 4 for a health phase signal.

2. Set up a Wireless latch on channel 5 and activate it when the transition animation ends.

3. In Signal logic, require channel 4 Powered AND channel 5 Powered, and output to channel 6.

4. Use channel 6 to trigger the phase particles. To test for a low input instead, change that row to Unpowered.
manual.sablelife.signal_logic.troublesho:
Check input channel modes, output channel mode, the module's trigger and Master power.

Deleting a channel unbinds its references rather than redirecting them to another channel. Presets require channels to be assigned again; local Copy retains them. Pulse progress is not kept through reload or blueprint placement.
manual.sablelife.combat_event.settings:
For Kills or Blocked attacks, each rule has a target filter, attack source, required count, output channel, strength, pulse duration and cooldown. Events required accepts 1â€“9,999 and defaults to 1. Reaching the count emits a pulse and resets the count for the next cycle.

Cooldown starts when output begins. Events during cooldown are ignored. Disabling or editing a rule clears its progress. Another output before a pulse ends extends the high signal; use a shorter pulse if receivers need distinct rising edges. Obsolete part-event rows are skipped when old data loads, while other rules are kept.

Own death emits once as the core enters its dying state, including after a one-hit kill or lethal Health adjustment. It requires an enabled Sequence-controlled external transmitter channel with red/blue frequencies. Filter, attack source, count and cooldown are not used for this event.

The death pulse belongs to the world's saved data after submission. It can continue after the core disappears and keeps its remaining duration through reload. It does not restart internal actions on the dying creature or keep its attack modules active.
manual.sablelife.combat_event.example:
1. For a block reaction, choose Blocked attacks, Events required 3 and cooldown 0. Every three confirmed blocks emit a pulse, then counting starts again.

2. For a kill reward, choose Kills, a player target filter and Events required 2. Every two attributed player kills emit a pulse. A respawned player can count again on a later death.

3. For a death signal, choose Own death and a configured external transmitter channel. Connect a separate external receiver to that frequency; the signal can outlast the original creature.
manual.sablelife.combat_event.troublesho:
For kill and block rules, enable Wireless and use a valid Sequence-controlled output channel. Only events attributed to this creature count. Canceled deaths, Creative or Spectator victims and kills by other attackers are excluded. Blocks need confirmation from a native shield or supported compatibility hook.

Own death specifically requires external transmission, not an internal channel on the dying core. Check both frequency items and the transmitter's enable state.

Ordinary counters and cooldowns are runtime-only. Events during cooldown are discarded. The submitted death pulse is the exception: it is stored independently in the world.

For Own death, choose an enabled Sequence-controlled external transmitter and set its red/blue frequencies. An internal-only output cannot survive the dying core. Kills and Blocked attacks can use their supported ordinary outputs.
core.sablelife.crush_help: Break actual world-block contacts while alive. Default delay is 0; support protection preserves floors. Terrain breaks before Travel step assist. Other Sable structures and unbreakable blocks are retained.
core.sablelife.crush_note: Break first, then step over protected obstacles. Debris is visual only.
core.sablelife.crushProtected_help: One block ID or #block_tag per entry. Listed blocks cannot be destroyed.
dashboard.sablelife.description_freeze: Shows a warning at a marked or sampled target position, then freezes eligible players or mobs inside the volume. Mechanical creatures are excluded.
dashboard.sablelife.freeze_help: Circle uses a cylinder; Rectangle uses length, width, height, angle and centered/ahead placement. Mark mode supports direction and start distance. The world-space warning volume is sampled once. Preview always draws the real volume, even with no warning particles selected. Leaving before activation avoids capture. Movement/jump/knockback are locked; look/attack/shield stay free. Freeze targets: players, ordinary mobs, or both. Mob AI/targeting/attacks continue; only movement is pinned. Sable lives are always excluded. On target supports Multiple target: off selects the nearest eligible target; on snapshots a separate warning volume at each eligible target (up to 64). All volumes share one warning/duration/cooldown, and overlapping volumes freeze each victim only once. Mark point hides this checkbox and keeps one volume.
manual.sablelife.freeze.settings:
Choose a release position. Mark point uses a mark on the structure; On target samples eligible target positions and needs no mark.

Circle uses radius 0.5â€“32 blocks and height 0.5â€“64. Rectangle uses length and width 0.5â€“64, height, an angle from -180 to 180 degrees, and centered or forward placement. Both shapes remain upright. A rectangle uses the marked face projected horizontally; On target uses world south plus the configured angle.

Mark mode also offers direction and Start distance from 0â€“128 blocks. The warning position and orientation are recorded once, so the warning does not follow a moving target.

Warning time accepts 0â€“60 seconds, freeze duration 0.05â€“60, and Interval 0.05â€“600. The interval runs after warning and freezing finish. The default Snowflake warning can be replaced. Preview outlines the actual volume regardless of the selected particles.

Freeze targets defaults to players; you can choose ordinary mobs or both. On target uses the same filter. Multiple target Off selects one eligible target using the core's target priority. On records a separate warning volume at each eligible target, up to 64. Those volumes share warning, duration and cooldown, and overlapping volumes freeze each victim only once. Mark point uses one volume and hides Multiple target.
manual.sablelife.freeze.example:
1. For a freezing roar, mark the mouth block. Try radius 10, warning 1 second and freeze duration 2 seconds.

2. Schedule Freeze and the roar sound in the same Move set. Keep Freeze's action window active through both warning and freezing.

3. Alternatively, choose On target without a mark. Test a fleeing player: the warning stays at the position recorded when the cast started.
manual.sablelife.freeze.troubleshooting:
Only eligible targets touching the volume when freezing starts are captured. Player targeting excludes Creative, Spectator and dead players. Mob targeting uses actual Mob entities and excludes mechanical creatures and armor stands.

Frozen mobs stay at their captured world position, but their AI, turning, targeting and attacks continue. Health, damage and status effects remain native; NoAI and NoGravity are not changed.

Different freeze sources have independent timers. Grab can carry a frozen target; if another freeze remains when Grab releases it, the target stays at its release position.

Losing the trigger, deleting the module, core unloading, death, entity unloading, dimension changes or timeout releases the relevant freeze source. Active freeze state is not saved.
dashboard.sablelife.description_grab: Captures an eligible player or ordinary mob near a marked mouth or hand, then carries it with that part. Mechanical creatures are excluded.
dashboard.sablelife.grab_help: Mark a mouth/hand face. Start distance offsets the held center along that face; side/height offsets rotate with the part. Nearest eligible player only. The player stays upright and can look, attack and shield. Warning/capture follows the Mark. Terrain obstruction, invalid/unloaded Mark, trigger off or timeout releases. Preview shows capture sphere (orange) and held player box (green). Target selector: players, ordinary mobs, or both. Mechanical Sable lives and armor stands are always excluded. Mob AI and movement logic continue normally; only position/velocity are constrained. NoAI/gravity flags are preserved.
manual.sablelife.grab.settings:
Mark one block on the intended mouth, hand or other part. Capture radius accepts 0.25â€“8 blocks, warning 0â€“60 seconds, hold time 0.05â€“60, and Interval 0.05â€“600 after warning and holding finish.

Start distance is 0â€“16 blocks along the marked face. Local side and height offsets accept -16 to 16. The hold point is the carried entity's body center, not its feet. Preview shows the capture sphere and an upright player-sized box.

The default Crit warning particles can be replaced. Capture targets defaults to players; choose ordinary mobs or both to include animals, monsters and other Mob entities.
manual.sablelife.grab.example:
1. For a bite, mark the mouth's outer face. Try Start distance 1.5, capture radius 1.5, warning 0.25 seconds and hold time 3 seconds.

2. Trigger the module. At the end of the warning it chooses an eligible target that is not already held, using the core's target priority. With the default Nearest priority, this is the closest eligible target.

3. Keep the module powered while a Move set animates the head. The captured target follows that part's position and rotation, but the player's view is not forcibly rotated.
manual.sablelife.grab.troubleshooting:
Player targets must be alive and in Survival or Adventure mode. Mob targeting uses real Mob entities. Mechanical Sable creatures, armor stands and decorative entities are excluded. One eligible target is captured per cast; targets already held are skipped.

Held mobs can still run their AI, target, attack and turn. Only position and velocity are constrained. Native health, damage, NoAI and gravity settings are unchanged. Player view, attack and shield behavior also remain available.

Death, source loss or removal, unloading, dimension changes, expiry or signal loss releases the attachment. Loaded-terrain and path checks still apply, including the maximum 8-block movement step. Mob tracking uses native synchronization. Addons with unusual movement overrides need in-game compatibility tests.
core.sablelife.crushProtected_preset_hel: Merge 20 common natural surface blocks, preserving existing entries and skipping duplicates. Up to 128 entries.
core.sablelife.crushProtected_picker_hel: Click an inventory block, then a sample slot; Shift-click adds directly. Right-click removes a sample. Confirm to register; items are not consumed.
dashboard.sablelife.impact_visual_help: Changes only impact visuals, never damage or warning radius. Set Color, Life and Size in the particle picker; Size scales individual particles. Spread follows damage radius or uses an independent 0â€“32 block radius. Count is the total shared across selections. Count 1 stays at the center; radius 0 centers all particles. An empty selection emits no impact particles. Flight particles remain separate.
dashboard.sablelife.description_summoned: Deploy independently aiming item weapons that follow a part or remain in the world; repeated activations append formations.
dashboard.sablelife.summon_finished: Expired; waiting for a new trigger
dashboard.sablelife.summon_help: Each activation deploys a group until each member expires; trigger loss or Move set completion does not cancel it. Reactivation appends a group. Death/release clears all; at most 256 active or pending weapons per core. Windup starts on each spawn and is included in lifetime (default 0); template warning times still apply. Default dispenser, starburst and firework launch; separate spawn/despawn particle and sound selectors. Preview shows the actual item, green model axes, orange muzzle mote and blue firing direction. Templates: Gun, Arrow, Flame, Laser, Slash, Ground strike, Quake, Attraction, Freeze, Shockwave and Grab. Summon owns the origin/aim/start offset; attack ranges and grab offsets remain. Released telegraphs lock their cast position. Shared target searches every 5 ticks; live aim and attacks update each tick. Preview uses the same native ItemDisplay renderer as the live weapon, including its Y-axis half-turn. Tracking preview uses the first turn step of a newly spawned weapon. Spawn/despawn media are at the end of the property list.
manual.sablelife.summoned_weapon.usage:
Summoned weapon creates visible weapons that use another attack module as a template. Add it, mark a structure part, choose an item and select an attack template. The template itself may be disabled and unmarked.

Each activation creates a separate group. Weapons stay until their configured lifetime expires, so repeated activations can leave several groups active at once.
manual.sablelife.summoned_weapon.setting:
Trigger loss or the end of a Move set action does not cancel spawned weapons or pending members of their group. A new activation adds another group. Death or Release clears all groups. Each core can have up to 256 active or pending weapons.

Windup starts when each weapon appears and counts toward its lifetime. It defaults to 0. The attack template's own warning or charge time still applies. Spawn and despawn have separate particle and sound selectors at the end of the property list; the default item is a dispenser, with starburst particles and a firework launch sound when it appears.

Supported templates are Gun, Arrow, Flamethrower, Laser, Slash, Ground strike, Earthquake wave, Attraction, Freeze, Shockwave and Grab. Summoned weapon supplies the origin, aim and starting offset. Attack ranges and Grab's offsets still come from the template. Released warnings keep their recorded cast positions.

Target searches are shared every 5 ticks, while aiming and attacks update each tick. Use Follow for a formation that follows the structure, or Fixed world position to leave it at the release location.

Preview shows the item, green model axes, an orange launch point and a blue firing direction. It uses the same item display rendering, including the model's Y-axis half-turn. Tracking Preview shows the first turn step of a newly spawned weapon.

A Move set can schedule Summoned weapon directly. Each action activation creates a new group; ending that action does not shorten the group's lifetime.
manual.sablelife.summoned_weapon.example:
1. Add Gun, set damage/interval/range, and disable it.

2. Add Summoned weapon, choose an item and reference that Gun.

3. Set Start distance 3, Follow, Track target and lifetime 5 seconds.

4. Correct model rotation with item XYZ and move the muzzle using local Z. Preview shows visual axes and the firing direction.

5. Trigger through Move set; select the original Gun as Hit counter source.

Formation example: count 5, vertical circle, radius 3, spawn interval 0.15 seconds and lifetime 5 seconds deploy a ring of floating weapons.

Multiple groups: use Fixed world position, lifetime 10 seconds and windup 0.5 seconds. Activate again every 2 seconds: older groups continue while new groups appear at the new launch positions.
manual.sablelife.summoned_weapon.trouble:
Holding the trigger high does not create groups continuously. Use a new rising edge or a new Move set activation for each group. Losing the trigger does not cancel a group's scheduled members.

If Windup is at least the lifetime, the weapon expires before it can attack. A viewer-only item Preview lasts about 3 seconds. Despawn particles and sounds are empty by default.

When a weapon expires, its attacks and any restraints it owns end. Other weapons and the original attack template are unaffected.

inspector.sablelife.title: Module manager
inspector.sablelife.missing_help: This reference points to a deleted module. Select a replacement in its editor.
inspector.sablelife.jump_help: Click to open the module or referenced Move Set move.
inspector.sablelife.group_count: %s modules. Click to assign the selected module to this group.
inspector.sablelife.source_help: Actual strength published by this module; simultaneous sources merge by maximum. Click to open.
inspector.sablelife.external_help: Actual received strength on this channel frequency. External transmitter identities are not available.
inspector.sablelife.latch_help: The channel retains this strength after its original source stops.

manual.sablelife.blueprint_spawn.setting:
File and placement
Server blueprint selects an approved file from server Sable-Schematics. Singleplayer uses its local game folder; this does not upload a remote client file.

Fixed world point stays in the world; Follow marked part uses its pose. Bottom center places the full bounds' lowest center at the destination; Saved blueprint origin uses its pivot. X/Y/Z offsets use world axes in fixed mode, part-local axes in follow mode.

Follow adds Direction/Start distance for translation. Top/bottom face marks do not automatically pitch the blueprint. Yaw/Pitch/Roll adjust orientation; fixed zero angles preserve the saved pose, explicit angles set its basis. Follow includes the part rotation.

Trigger and limit
A rising trigger submits one job, subject to cooldown and this module's generation limit across the current core activation. Limit 2 means two completed generations total, not two per pulse; Release/reactivation resets it. Delay postpones a submitted job. Activate core needs one ordinary Heart Core and no Redstone Core; Off permits pure structures.

For death generation, route an Own death Combat Event output to this module's trigger. The job freezes the destination at death and waits for cleanup/delay. Release cancels queued work but retains the selected template; Clear removes it. Copies need operator selection again.

Preview
Only the requesting player sees cyan bounds and a projection within the server limit. It places nothing and does not validate terrain clearance. A submitted job shows its frozen destination.
manual.sablelife.blueprint_spawn.example:
Select a server blueprint. In fixed mode, mark the ground and keep Bottom center to place the full blueprint above that point. Adjust Generation offset Y to raise or lower it, then use Yaw/Pitch/Roll and Preview to check the projected structure.

For moving launch points, choose Follow marked part, mark one connected block and set Direction/Start distance. Use local X/Y/Z offsets to fine-tune the point without changing orientation. A top-face mark can move the point upward while the blueprint remains upright.

Use an Own death Combat Event on the blueprint trigger's channel to generate a replacement after cleanup. The world position and orientation freeze when the job is submitted, even if its original part later disappears.
manual.sablelife.blueprint_spawn.trouble:
Server blueprint lists server-local files, not a remote player upload list. Only an operator can select templates. Automatic activation requires exactly one Heart Core and no Redstone Core. Imported command modules keep their approval restrictions.

Use Preview to check the full bounds, anchor and projected structure. If the blueprint is underground, choose Bottom center or increase Generation offset Y. A rotated blueprint is anchored using its rotated lowest bound.

Release retains the selected template and resets runtime counters, cooldown and pending work. Arena recordings are retained too; re-record Arena if the build or its settings have changed. Releasing does not remove already completed independent blueprint spawns. Clear explicitly removes a template. Copying a module does not copy its server registration.

Generation still requires loaded chunks and obeys server limits. Incomplete placement fails without automatic retry; partial generated bodies are rolled back where possible. Preview is not a terrain collision check.

dashboard.sablelife.description_entity_h: Creates an invisible living damage receiver at a marked structure block. Choose entity-only or hybrid entity/structure damage. Both use the Heart Core health and part defenses.
dashboard.sablelife.hitbox_help: Uses the first valid triggered receivers up to the server limit (default 8). Entity only disables direct structure damage. Hybrid enables both routes for the whole creature while at least one hybrid receiver is active. For a continuous receiver, use Always. Positions follow parts; boxes stay world-axis-aligned. The marked part supplies armor. Preview shows the box; death, Release, unload or disabling removes it. Hybrid deduplicates identifiable sources; unusual mod attacks may need adapters. Enable Attract hostile mobs to let nearby hostile mobs and mobs with retaliation goals select this receiver before taking damage. Existing targets take priority. Passive animals without those goals remain passive.
manual.sablelife.entity_hitbox.settings:
Mark a block on the intended part. Width, Height and Depth are 0.25â€“16 blocks; local X/Y/Z offsets are -16 to 16. The server permits the first 8 valid, triggered receivers by default. maximumEntityHitboxesPerCreature can change this to 1â€“32.

New modules default to Hybrid: entity + structure. Entity only disables direct structure damage while valid receivers exist. If any active receiver uses Hybrid, both damage paths are enabled for the whole creature. Both share core health and the marked part's defenses. Existing mode choices are preserved.

Always keeps receivers active during the creature's life, subject to valid marks, module/server switches, triggers and Master. When none remain, normal structure-only damage returns. Death, Release and unloading remove the receivers; loaded eligible cores recreate them as needed.

The position and local offset follow the part's rotation, but each actual hitbox stays aligned with world axes and does not tilt. Use several small boxes for long moving limbs.

Attract hostile mobs lets nearby hostile mobs and mobs with retaliation goals acquire a receiver before taking damage. Existing targets take priority. Passive animals without attack goals remain passive. Retaliation after being damaged is separate and does not require this switch.
manual.sablelife.entity_hitbox.example:
1. Mark a block on a leg and use a small box to cover the intended hit area. Add a second module for the head if needed.

2. Preview each box and adjust its dimensions and offsets. Part damage modifiers use the part that owns each mark. Sable Life's own target selectors still treat the whole creature as one target, rather than several mobs.

3. With receivers active, let the creature damage a mob that normally retaliates. If the attack has no real living attacker, Sable Life can supply one of its receivers. The mob's existing retaliation AI may then pursue and attack it. Retaliation after damage works independently of the Attract hostile mobs switch.

4. For its first retaliation target, the mob receives the nearest valid box, measured to the box boundary rather than its center. Later hits from that creature keep the same receiver while it remains valid. If it becomes invalid, the next damaging hit selects a new one.

5. Keep at least one receiver low enough for ground melee mobs. Selection does not check reachability; normal targeting, range and pathfinding limits still apply.
manual.sablelife.entity_hitbox.troublesh:
Damage route
Receivers are invisible living entities with no AI, pushing, loot or separate health. Loaded cores recreate them; they are not saved. Damage uses core defenses. Solid terrain can block weapons before they reach a box: offset/enlarge it if needed.

Hybrid deduplication
Hits settle at tick end. Identified projectiles transfer once per creature across body/receiver routes; a queued receiver hit may be replaced by body contact. Immune body contact still consumes it. Same-attacker melee aliases merge within a tick; different attackers remain separate. Native explosions use the highest part-adjusted contact once per explosion; marked cosmetic spell blasts add no second hit.

Post-damage events report actual core health lost once; incoming/pre-damage hooks run at contact. Continuous body APIs keep their own cadence. Missing/different source IDs or unrelated same-caster attacks may need adapters. Not every weapon, target filter or post-hit effect is supported. Hybrid is experimental; try Entity only for a problematic weapon.

Cannot reach the core?
In Creative, right-click any active receiver with the Creative Release Tool, including in the off hand. It releases that creature even if the box covers the core. Ordinary interaction does not release it.

manual.sablelife.getting_started.step_as:
1. Build and assemble

Place one Heart Core in a small structure. Add a block to use as the firing point, then assemble the build with Sable. Keep only one core across all connected parts. Placing blocks on ordinary terrain alone does not assemble them.

The dispenser icon is only an example of a firing block. Any valid structure block can be marked; an actual dispenser is not required.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.step_da:
2. Add one attack

Right-click the core with an empty hand. In Modules, click + Add, select Arrow launcher and load it. Select the new module. Keep Straight aiming and Trigger: Always for this first test. Apply edited numbers with the checkmark or Enter.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.step_ma:
3. Mark the firing face

Click Mark area/origin. In the world, right-click the face of the structure block that should fire outward. The mark chooses the firing part and direction; it does not select a player or mob to attack. A successful mark returns to the editor.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.step_pr:
4. Check the launch point

Set Start distance to 1 block as a starting point, then click Preview. Check that the muzzle is outside the structure and the direction points outward. Adjust it if needed. Preview only shows the configured result; it does not fire an arrow or deal damage.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.step_ac:
5. Activate and test

Close the menu. Sneak-right-click the core with an empty hand to activate it. Keep the muzzle clear and test against an eligible mob in front of it. Always now supplies the trigger. For later target-aimed modules, check target type, range and visibility separately.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.step_re:
6. Release before changing locked settings

Use Release in the dashboard, or right-click the creature with the Creative Release Tool while in Creative mode. This returns it to dormant editing and keeps the structure and saved settings. Release stops current actions and clears runtime state. After editing, check the marks and activate again; modules restart according to their trigger conditions.

manual.sablelife.survival_heart_core.usa:
The Survival Heart Core gives a Sable structure health and modules in Survival mode. Energy pays for health, healing, attacks and certain control abilities. It is separate from the ordinary Heart Core and Redstone Core.

Empty-hand right-click opens it. Configure while dormant, refuel it, complete marks, then sneak-right-click with an empty hand to activate. Current Life shows the stored health before activation and the current health while active.
manual.sablelife.survival_heart_core.set:
Refuel shows the server's accepted materials and Energy value per item. Hover an item to read its value, place real items in the input slots, then confirm twice. Confirmation consumes those items. Closing before confirmation returns unspent inputs. A normally mined core item retains its remaining Energy. Remaining life is preserved by Release, not by mining the core; ordinary blueprints reset both to zero to prevent copying paid resources. Each server supplies its own prices.

Activation tries to restore missing health and pays only for that difference. If Energy is insufficient but some life remains, activation can use that remaining life instead. Zero life requires enough Energy to restore it. Healing charges for health actually restored and is limited by the available Energy.

The golden estimate and ? beside each module show the current server's formula. Melee charges per successful hit; most attacks pay per release, and repeated releases pay again. Armor reduction is capped at 90% and is billed per active second, even without incoming hits. The default is 1 Energy per percentage point per second: 90% costs 90/s. A spawned weapon can also pay for its referenced attack.

Loot, death XP, command, Arena and Blueprint generation are unavailable. Potion-effect attributes are removed; native burning and visual effects are separate. Adaptive defense, collision terrain breaking, void-height death, force chunk loading and detached-part cleanup are unavailable. Other-Life damage is always accepted, Survival interaction is always allowed, and permitted player mining drops blocks. Settings that are fixed are hidden.

Health reaching zero plays the life-depleted effect and automatically releases the structure; it does not run the ordinary death-delay/removal/reward process. Release keeps remaining life and Energy. An active ordinary Heart Core cannot be released with the Survival Release Tool.
manual.sablelife.survival_heart_core.exa:
1. Craft the Redstone Core recipe with redstone dust in the center instead of the amethyst shard. Assemble it in a small Sable structure.

2. Open Refuel, inspect the listed values and insert accepted materials. Confirm twice.

3. Set maximum health to 100. At the default 1 Energy/HP, a fresh 0/100 core needs 100 Energy for full health.

4. Add one attack, mark it and check its estimate. Activate, test one release, then inspect Energy and Current Life.

5. Before changing locked settings, use Release or right-click the creature with the Survival Release Tool. This tool only works with Survival Heart Cores. Release keeps remaining life and Energy; reactivation still charges for missing health.
manual.sablelife.survival_heart_core.tro:
Insufficient Energy can prevent a paid release or healing; an enabled trigger is not proof of payment. Estimates depend on the current settings and server rates, not only the Damage field. Blast radius, speed, range, duration, projectile count and repeated ground-strike points can change the price.

Player names, owners and factions control target selection; they do not grant editor permissions. This core is editable by Survival players who can build and interact there. Server protections can still reject interaction.

Check [modules.survivalHeartCore] for skill switches and [survivalTokens] for material values and rates. Internal config/data keys may retain Token names; the displayed resource is Energy. Do not use the ordinary-core Survival-editing switch as a requirement for this core.

Target aiming for Arrow launcher, Gun, Mortar and Slash fires from the marked muzzle; it does not place the attack on the target. Direct target-position spawning of area skills remains unavailable. These aimed shots still use the server's Energy charges.
manual.sablelife.natural_spawning.usage:
The Wild Encounter Tool lets an operator choose server blueprints and spawn them around nearby players. Rules are saved on the server, including tracked objects across restarts. Creative players can trigger automatic searches; Spectators cannot.

Density controls search frequency and distance. There is no separate percentage chance: a valid candidate can spawn when cooldowns and population limits allow it. Random positions and failed checks affect how often you actually see a spawn.
manual.sablelife.natural_spawning.settin:
Load and enable
Add a rule, choose a server blueprint and Load. Activate core: Yes requires one ordinary Heart Core and no Redstone Core; No permits pure structures. Set Conditions, then Enable.

Density and population
Density sets success cooldown, failed-search retry, candidates per search and player distance. All rules share at most one search round per second, stopping after success. There is no separate percentage chance.

Max present limits this rule. Server defaults: 64 tracked objects across all rules/dimensions, 4 within 128 blocks. Unloaded objects count; these caps do not multiply. Current shows the tracked number.

Cleanup
Lifetime counts server game time; 0 disables it. No-player cleanup starts with no living non-Spectator within 128 blocks; returning resets it. Either timer can request removal, even with self chunk loading. Unloaded objects retain deadlines and are removed when required data loads. Pure structures follow the same rules.

Release after spawning detaches new objects from counts, timers and Clear all current. Lifetime 0 alone does not release them.

Terrain
Ground clearance lifts the blueprint. Require open sky rejects cover. Water below a flying build is allowed if outside its checked volume. Loaded terrain, world bounds and other applicable checks remain.

Skip full blueprint bounds check tests occupied volumes instead of the enclosing box. Clear obstacles can cut terrain/buildings inside the bounds; ownership, block entities, unbreakable blocks and budgets can block it. Workbench protection still applies.

Biomes, faction and announcement
Empty biomes means any. Overworld includes non-ocean Overworld biomes, including correctly tagged modded ones; add oceans explicitly. Wilds is the hidden default faction and does not automatically attack itself.

An announcement broadcasts after every successful spawn, including Test spawn and released objects. Blank disables it. Coords appends the actual blueprint bottom-center coordinates; it defaults Off and clears with blank text.

Announcements support &0â€“&f colors, &l bold, &o italic, &n underline, &m strikethrough, &k obfuscated, &r reset and &#RRGGBB hex colors. Example: &e&lMachine has arrived! Formatting codes count toward the 256-character limit.
manual.sablelife.natural_spawning.exampl:
1. Add a rule, select a small server blueprint and Load. Choose whether to activate its core.

2. Set ground clearance, allowed biomes, faction and a low population limit. Set Lifetime and No-player cleanup, or deliberately choose Release after spawning.

3. Use Preview ahead to inspect bounds and projection. Reopen the tool to return to that rule. A blocked preview may still be visible and will show a reason.

4. Use Test spawn for actual placement, then check Current in the list. Enable the rule to test automatic spawning around a non-Spectator player.

5. Use Clear all current to remove this rule's tracked objects. The red X deletes the rule after a second confirmation; it is separate from clearing spawned objects.
manual.sablelife.natural_spawning.troubl:
If nothing spawns, read the Test spawn failure reason. Check master config, rule enable state, cooldown, all population caps, loaded footprint, biome, sky, water/obstacles and build height. Large blueprints can fail where small ones fit. Raising ground clearance does not fix an unloaded footprint or every other failure.

An empty allowed-biome list permits every biome; the Overworld group excludes ocean types. More candidates improve search opportunities, not guaranteed success. The limits count pure structures too, and include tracked unloaded objects.

Set enableWildEncounters=false in the server config to stop automatic spawning, Test spawn and managed expiry cleanup while preserving saved rules. Already placed structures are not deleted and active creatures can keep running. Large native blueprint placement can pause the server; a configurable cap is not a performance guarantee.
manual.sablelife.block_interaction.usage: Simulates an empty-hand right-click on the nearest supported block in a small area. Mark the reference part, then choose World interaction or Structure interaction. It does not attack entities or open inventory screens.
manual.sablelife.block_interaction.setti:
Size defaults to 1 and accepts 1â€“3: a 1Ã—1Ã—1 to 3Ã—3Ã—3 search cube. Only the nearest supported block to the reference point is used each time, not every block in that cube.

Start distance moves the point along the marked face. X/Y/Z offsets use the marked part's local axes. In World mode, the point follows the moving part but searches ordinary world blocks. Structure mode searches only the marked rigid body's own blocks.

Once runs on a new trigger or Move set activation. Repeat uses the configured interval while triggered. Supported targets are vanilla wooden doors/trapdoors, fence gates, buttons and levers. Iron doors/trapdoors, containers, crafting tables and other mods' blocks are ignored. Preview outlines the search area and highlights the currently chosen block in white.
manual.sablelife.block_interaction.examp:
1. Mark a block on a moving hand. Choose World interaction, size 1 and Once.

2. Set Start distance and offsets so Preview's cube covers a world lever.

3. Trigger once to toggle it. For an onboard lever instead, select Structure interaction and place the search cube over a lever on the same rigid body.

4. Use Repeat only when repeated clicks are intended: a lever or door can toggle back again.
manual.sablelife.block_interaction.troub:
The marked block is a reference, not necessarily the block that gets clicked. The search cube must cover a supported target in the selected space. A target on another connected rigid body is not part of Structure mode's search.

Server interaction protection or a canceled interaction event can reject the click. This module uses its own simulated player; it does not impersonate the named Owner or bypass claims.
manual.sablelife.combat_compatibility.us: These notes describe explicitly supported native damage paths. They do not promise every spell, weapon or entity-only event will recognize a Sable body. Entity hitbox is a separate optional module; the adapters below do not require it.

manual.sablelife.getting_started.automat:
Automation: three controls to learn
Move set selects moves using conditions, priority and weight; its action windows schedule supported attack, movement, sound and function modules.

Wireless Channel is the core's channel page. Internal numbers belong to this core; external reception uses matching red/blue frequency items. A channel number is not a global wireless frequency.

Wireless Redstone turns a trigger into marked-face redstone, external frequency output or an internal signal. It can turn a Move set action window into input for another module.

First combination

1. Enable channel 1 as Sequence / internal; keep wireless Master On.

2. Give Move set the Always trigger and Ignore conditions. Add a Wireless Redstone action from 0 to 2 seconds.

3. Set that module to Move set trigger, Continuous output, Invert Off, internal output channel 1. It needs no marked output face or frequency items.

4. Let an enabled, marked Particle effects module with a selected particle read internal channel 1. It emits in that window; old particles finish their lifetimes afterward.

Then read Move set, Triggers and signals, and Wireless Redstone. Keep input/output channels separate while learning to avoid feedback.

manual.sablelife.natural_spawning.workbe:
Workbench protection
Fixed-world vanilla crafting tables block spawning within 64 horizontal blocks of the entire blueprint footprint, at every height. Test spawn, bounds-skip and clearing obey it. Tables on moving Sable structures do not carry this zone.

Server config wildWorkbenchProtectionRadius accepts 0-256; 0 disables it. This excludes spawns, not existing creature movement, damage or editor access, and does not cover every modded workbench.

Chunks are indexed in budgeted batches; later table changes update the cache. Verified records survive unload/restart. Unknown or evicted records wait for loaded verification, without forcing chunks. A pending message may mean surrounding terrain is unloaded. Removing the last table in a column removes its protection.
manual.sablelife.wireless_channels.usage:
Open Wireless Channel from the module dashboard. It is the core's signal panel, not the Wireless Redstone module. Keep Master and the selected channels enabled. Heart Cores need life activation; assembled Redstone Cores run without it.

Channel numbers belong to this core. Core A channel 1 and core B channel 1 are unrelated. External links match ordered red/blue frequency items instead, so A channel 1 can talk to B channel 7. Samples are not consumed.
manual.sablelife.wireless_channels.setti:
Choose a channel mode
Internal repeat: generate a local waveform using Delay, On, Off, Strength and Loop. No frequency items needed.

External receive / RX: listen for matching external frequency items. Modules read this with External RX, not Internal wireless.

External output / TX: transmit the timed waveform through matching frequency items. Its output can also be read internally.

Sequence / internal: accept output from signal-producing modules, rather than generating a waveform. Internal wireless reads it; no frequency items needed.

Sequence / external TX: accept those module outputs and transmit them externally. Internal readers can use the same output. External modes need at least one frequency item; both slots, including empty slots, must match the other end.

Latch and names
Latch holds a nonzero output until its Reset channel fires; reset wins, and input must go low before relatching. It is for output channels, not RX, and runtime state resets on reload. Names are cosmetic (up to 40 characters); Enter/checkmark saves without restarting the signal.
manual.sablelife.wireless_channels.examp:
Inside -> inside
Enable channel 1 as Sequence / internal. Let a signal module write channel 1; set the receiving module to Internal wireless, channel 1. For a Move set action, use Wireless Redstone as the signal producer.

Inside -> outside
Set that output channel to Sequence / external TX and choose red/blue frequency A. Put the same ordered items on an external Create Redstone Link in receive mode. Alternatively, Wireless Redstone can transmit directly from its own frequency slots, without an output channel.

Outside -> inside
A powered external Create Redstone Link transmits frequency A. Set core channel 1 to External receive / RX with A. Set the consuming module to External RX, channel 1. Keep both ends loaded, in the same dimension and within Create's link range.

Need a local copy? Let Wireless Redstone read External RX channel 1 and write channel 2 (Sequence / internal). Other modules then read Internal wireless channel 2.

Outside -> outside
Use that RX channel as Wireless Redstone's trigger. Set its own frequency slots to a different frequency B, Continuous output, Invert Off; choose Follow input to preserve strength. A receiver matching B gets the relayed signal. No marked face or internal output channel is required.
manual.sablelife.wireless_channels.troub:
RX input and channel output are separate. An RX channel can show received power while Internal wireless reads zero: use External RX or the local-copy bridge above.

Match frequency items and red/blue order, not names or channel numbers. Check Master, channel enable, core operation, Create link range and loaded chunks. A module may still need its own valid mark.

Multiple producers combine by highest strength. Give relay inputs/outputs different channels and frequencies to prevent feedback. Output binding 0 means unbound.

Internal repeat and External output / TX generate waveforms; both Sequence modes need a producer. A short pulse may end before a slow action runs. See Wireless Redstone for Pulse, Reverse and Ramp.

manual.sablelife.melee.brief_usage: Damages targets inside a marked melee area, with adjustable reach and attack timing.
manual.sablelife.melee.brief_example: Add Melee, mark the attack area and set its damage. Use Always for a first test, then activate with a valid target inside the area.
manual.sablelife.melee.brief_troubleshoo: Check that the mark belongs to a connected part, the target matches the filter and the trigger is active. Survival cores also need enough Energy.
manual.sablelife.flame.brief_usage: Projects a damaging flame stream with particle effects from the marked muzzle, using a cone or fan pattern.
manual.sablelife.flame.brief_example: Mark a muzzle facing open space, choose Cone or Fan and set damage. Use Always, activate and test a target in front.
manual.sablelife.flame.brief_troubleshoo: If the flame points the wrong way, check the marked face and firing angles. If it does not fire or hurt, check the trigger, target filter and Energy balance.
manual.sablelife.arrow.brief_usage: Fires arrows or custom item-model projectiles from a marked muzzle, with straight or target-aimed shots.
manual.sablelife.arrow.brief_example: Add Arrow launcher, mark the muzzle and start with straight aim and Always. Activate, confirm the flight path, then choose a custom appearance if wanted.
manual.sablelife.arrow.brief_troubleshoo: Keep the muzzle clear of the machine. Target aim needs an eligible target; custom item size and rotation change appearance, not damage.
manual.sablelife.gun.brief_usage: Fires fast projectiles from a marked muzzle, with custom item appearances and optional impact explosions.
manual.sablelife.gun.brief_example: Mark an outward-facing muzzle, choose straight aim and set damage. Use Always and activate; test a short clear firing lane first.
manual.sablelife.gun.brief_troubleshooti: If shots hit the machine, adjust the muzzle start distance. For missing target-aimed shots, check range, target filters and Energy.
manual.sablelife.mortar.brief_usage: Launches arcing projectiles toward targets, with optional impact explosions and lingering damage areas.
manual.sablelife.mortar.brief_example: Mark a launch face, choose a target type and set damage. Activate with a target in range and enough overhead space for the arc.
manual.sablelife.mortar.brief_troublesho: A target may be in search range but unreachable with the selected launch settings. Check overhead obstacles, launch speed and angle, then Energy.
manual.sablelife.surface_field.brief_usa: Defines a lingering damage-area template that other attacks place at their impact points.
manual.sablelife.surface_field.brief_exa: Add Persistent area damage and set its shape, damage and duration. Select this template in an attack's impact-area option, then trigger that attack.
manual.sablelife.surface_field.brief_tro: This template does not cast on its own. Check that the attacking module references it and actually lands a hit; also check its target filter and Energy.
manual.sablelife.homing.brief_usage: Deploys a formation of hovering projectiles that charge and launch toward eligible targets.
manual.sablelife.homing.brief_example: Mark the deployment face, choose an item appearance and target type, then set damage. Activate with a target in range and watch deployment before launch.
manual.sablelife.homing.brief_troublesho: Deployment and launch are separate stages. If it never launches, check the target, line of sight, trigger and Energy; an empty appearance can also hide the model.
manual.sablelife.laser.brief_usage: Fires a laser beam with target tracking and horizontal or vertical sweeping.
manual.sablelife.laser.brief_example: Mark a muzzle, select a beam style and set length and damage. Use Always and activate; add a sweep angle and speed after the fixed beam works.
manual.sablelife.laser.brief_troubleshoo: Check the muzzle direction and trigger first. Missing custom effects need selected particles; dense particles can leave trails even when the beam itself follows the part.
manual.sablelife.sphere_blast.brief_usag: Charges a sphere in front of the marked face, then releases one area explosion.
manual.sablelife.sphere_blast.brief_exam: Mark a forward-facing origin and set the distance, blast radius and damage. Trigger it in clear space and confirm the charge finishes before the blast.
manual.sablelife.sphere_blast.brief_trou: The sphere stays at its planned cast position. Check charge time, trigger and Energy if no blast occurs; terrain destruction has its own permissions.
manual.sablelife.slash.brief_usage: Launches traveling arc-shaped slashes, with adjustable size, spread, color and effects.
manual.sablelife.slash.brief_example: Mark an outward-facing muzzle, set damage and a short range, then use Always. Activate in clear space and adjust the arc's orientation after it fires.
manual.sablelife.slash.brief_troubleshoo: Check the marked face and roll angle if the arc looks sideways. Display size alone does not guarantee a hit; check the flight path, target filter and Energy.
manual.sablelife.ground_strike.brief_usa: Creates ground strikes along configured lines or scattered points, with optional falling-item visuals.
manual.sablelife.ground_strike.brief_exa: Choose a release origin and strike pattern, then set damage and a few strike points. Trigger on open ground and check the warning positions before expanding it.
manual.sablelife.ground_strike.brief_tro: Strikes need a valid ground surface. Item appearance, size and rotation are visual only; check strike positions, target filters and Energy when damage is missing.
manual.sablelife.quake.brief_usage: Sends damaging earthquake waves across the ground in straight, ring or area patterns.
manual.sablelife.quake.brief_example: Mark the origin, choose a wave pattern and set range and damage. Activate on flat ground with a target standing in the wave's path.
manual.sablelife.quake.brief_troubleshoo: Ground rules can exclude airborne targets or interrupt propagation. Check the surface, target filter, trigger and Energy before increasing the range.
manual.sablelife.pull.brief_usage: Pulls nearby targets into a sphere or directional funnel, with direct pulling or stable intake.
manual.sablelife.pull.brief_example: For a first test, mark the origin, choose a target type and use a small sphere. Activate near a valid target, then switch to a funnel and adjust its direction if needed.
manual.sablelife.pull.brief_troubleshoot: Targets inside the stop distance stop moving by design. Target-position casts use a sphere; a directional funnel needs marked-origin mode.
manual.sablelife.freeze.brief_usage: Warns and then freezes eligible players or ordinary mobs inside a circular or rectangular area.
manual.sablelife.freeze.brief_example: Mark an origin, choose a small area and set warning and freeze times. Activate with a valid target inside the marked area.
manual.sablelife.freeze.brief_troublesho: Sable Life creatures are excluded. Check target filters, area height and warning timing; a target-position cast also needs an eligible target in search range.
manual.sablelife.grab.brief_usage: Captures a nearby player or ordinary mob and holds it at a point that follows the marked part.
manual.sablelife.grab.brief_example: Mark a hand or mouth, set a small capture radius and holding time, then activate near a target. Preview the holding point before using it on a large machine.
manual.sablelife.grab.brief_troubleshoot: Sable Life creatures are excluded. The nearest eligible target must enter capture range; check offsets, trigger and Energy if nothing is caught.
manual.sablelife.pulse.brief_usage: Releases an area pulse that damages and knocks back nearby eligible targets.
manual.sablelife.pulse.brief_example: Mark an origin, set a small radius, damage and knockback, then activate near a target. Use the expanding visual if you want a visible shockwave.
manual.sablelife.pulse.brief_troubleshoo: A visible wave does not bypass target filtering. Check release position, trigger, interval and Energy if the pulse does not affect a target.
manual.sablelife.summoned_weapon.brief_u: Deploys floating item-model weapons in a formation and lets them use a linked attack template.
manual.sablelife.summoned_weapon.brief_e: Choose a weapon item, mark a deployment part and select an attack module as its template. Trigger deployment with a valid target nearby.
manual.sablelife.summoned_weapon.brief_t: The attack template can stay disabled and unmarked, but must still exist and be allowed. Check weapon lifetime, target selection and Energy if deployed weapons do not attack.
manual.sablelife.arena.brief_usage: Defines a fixed arena and handles the creature leaving it, with optional return and recorded-structure restoration.
manual.sablelife.arena.brief_example: Mark the arena center, set its radius and choose the out-of-bounds response. Record the current structure if using restoration, then activate and test near the boundary.
manual.sablelife.arena.brief_troubleshoo: The creature leaving the arena starts the warning, not a player leaving. Restoration needs a current structure record; also check nearby-player and server permissions.
manual.sablelife.armor.brief_usage: Changes incoming damage for a marked part or the whole creature through signal-controlled rules.
manual.sablelife.armor.brief_example: Choose whole-creature scope or mark a part. Add a negative modifier rule, bind an existing channel and supply the signal it requires, then activate and test damage.
manual.sablelife.armor.brief_troubleshoo: Enabling the module does not bypass its rule conditions. Missing or unbound channels do not activate protection; Survival Heart Cores also need enough Energy.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.brief_u: Moves connected machine parts by teleporting after a charge or traveling along a route, with optional gravity and step assist.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.brief_e: Mark the movement direction, choose Travel and a short distance. Bind an internal channel, Preview, activate and supply that channel's signal.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.brief_t: Check the trigger and collision result first. Connected bodies still use conservative bounds, and unloaded destinations block movement; target movement also needs a valid target.
manual.sablelife.auto_facing.brief_usage: Turns the connected creature toward an eligible target, using the marked face as its front.
manual.sablelife.auto_facing.brief_examp: Mark a clear front face, choose a target type and use Always. Activate with a target in range; enable vertical tracking only if needed.
manual.sablelife.auto_facing.brief_troub: Check target range and filters first, then collision and other motion controllers. A vertical marked face cannot define horizontal-only facing.
manual.sablelife.signal_turn.brief_usage: Turns connected machine parts from six directional wireless inputs, with analog strength controlling the turn.
manual.sablelife.signal_turn.brief_examp: Mark the front face and bind one turning direction to a channel. Activate and vary that channel's signal, then add the other directions.
manual.sablelife.signal_turn.brief_troub: Unbound channels do not turn the machine. Check wireless Master, input source and collisions; another motion controller may currently own rotation.
manual.sablelife.gyroscope.brief_usage: Records a reference posture and smoothly rights connected parts when tilt exceeds the limit.
manual.sablelife.gyroscope.brief_example: Mark a fixed main-body part and record its current posture as level. Set a tilt limit and recovery mode, then activate and tip the machine to test.
manual.sablelife.gyroscope.brief_trouble: The tilt limit and righting speed apply to both recovery modes. Check calibration, trigger, collision and rotation locks; this module provides no lift.
manual.sablelife.particles.brief_usage: Creates decorative particle effects in areas, points, lines, rings or spheres.
manual.sablelife.particles.brief_example: Choose a particle and pattern, mark the required point or area and use Always. Activate and adjust the appearance after the first effect appears.
manual.sablelife.particles.brief_trouble: An empty particle selection is invisible. Check that marks match the chosen pattern; particles are visual and do not cause attack damage.
manual.sablelife.health_bar.brief_usage: Displays a red health bar and optional creature name at a marked point, following the part and facing each viewer.
manual.sablelife.health_bar.brief_exampl: Mark a visible point above the machine and choose Always visible for a first test. Activate, then adjust bar size and optional name size.
manual.sablelife.health_bar.brief_troubl: Check visibility mode and view distance. Terrain can hide the bar, and a blank core name hides the name text.
manual.sablelife.item_display.brief_usag: Shows an item model at a marked point as decoration, without creating a pickup or damage source.
manual.sablelife.item_display.brief_exam: Choose an item, mark its attachment point and set a small display size. Activate or enable the module's always-display option, then adjust rotation.
manual.sablelife.item_display.brief_trou: Check the item selection, valid mark and display conditions. This visual model has no collision and cannot be collected.
manual.sablelife.trigger_sound.brief_usa: Plays a selected sound mix when triggered, with optional marked-block contact detection.
manual.sablelife.trigger_sound.brief_exa: Choose a sound and Preview it. Select trigger playback or mark a contact block, then activate and test that event.
manual.sablelife.trigger_sound.brief_tro: An empty mix is silent. Check contact mode, trigger and replay behavior; hearing range is separate from the contact-detection area.
manual.sablelife.sound.brief_usage: Plays creature sounds for approach, hurt and ambient events.
manual.sablelife.sound.brief_example: Open one event's sound selector, add a sound and Preview it. Activate, then reproduce that event before configuring the others.
manual.sablelife.sound.brief_troubleshoo: Check the event's detection range and cooldown, not only hearing range. Empty mixes are silent.
manual.sablelife.bgm.brief_usage: Plays creature music with trigger, distance and fade controls.
manual.sablelife.bgm.brief_example: Choose a music track, Preview it and set a modest hearing range. Activate under the selected start condition and test from nearby.
manual.sablelife.bgm.brief_troubleshooti: Check the start condition and hearing range. Leave or release the creature to verify stopping; multiple nearby music sources can compete.
manual.sablelife.loot.brief_usage: Assigns loot rewards to a marked part when it detaches, with quantity and chance controls.
manual.sablelife.loot.brief_example: Mark the loot-bearing part, open its loot editor and copy in an item sample. Set a quantity, then activate and detach that part to test.
manual.sablelife.loot.brief_troubleshoot: An empty sample or zero quantity produces nothing. Check that the marked part actually detached and that the core permits this module.
manual.sablelife.hover_anchor.brief_usag: Holds a marked point in place while connected parts can move or sway around it.
manual.sablelife.hover_anchor.brief_exam: Mark a stable point on the main body, choose the axes to hold and activate. Add rotation locking only if you want the posture held too.
manual.sablelife.hover_anchor.brief_trou: A fixed point is not a lock on every block. Check held axes, offsets and rotation locking if the machine sways or another movement controller waits.
manual.sablelife.health_adjustment.brief: Heals or damages the creature itself when triggered, for recovery skills or self-damage costs.
Set a small positive amount for healing or a negative amount for self-damage. Bind a controlled trigger, activate and send one test signal.
Healing cannot exceed maximum health. Check trigger timing and cooldown; Survival Heart Cores need Energy for actual healing.
manual.sablelife.visual_shockwave.brief_: Shows gathering, mechanical rings, shield fragments, exhaust, planar fissures, echoes or symbols at a mark. It also provides screen distortion, shake, zoom and color effects for nearby players.
Mark a muzzle, choose Mechanical rings or Symbols, then set color, size and duration. Bind a short trigger and use Follow marked part to test it while the structure moves.

Check the mark, trigger, range and duration. Walls occlude patterns; symbols face the camera. Fissures lie on the marked plane without changing terrain. Following stops if the part unloads or its marked block is destroyed.
manual.sablelife.distortion_trail.brief_: Leaves a fading ribbon of air distortion behind a moving or swinging marked part.
Mark a moving limb, enable the trail and activate. Move or swing that part, then adjust ribbon size after confirming the trail.
A stationary part may produce no new trail. Check the movement threshold, trigger and client visual settings; this effect causes no damage.
manual.sablelife.blueprint_spawn.brief_u: Spawns a selected server blueprint at a fixed world point or a point following the marked part.
manual.sablelife.blueprint_spawn.brief_e: Select and load a server blueprint, choose its position mode and mark the location. Preview, adjust placement and trigger once.
manual.sablelife.blueprint_spawn.brief_t: Check that the blueprint still exists, placement is allowed and the activation limit is not reached. Activating a spawned core requires a valid core inside the blueprint.
manual.sablelife.entity_hitbox.brief_usa: Adds invisible entity damage receivers that forward hits to the creature's shared health and part defenses.
manual.sablelife.entity_hitbox.brief_exa: Mark the receiving part, size the box around it and keep Hybrid for a first test. Preview, activate and hit the box with a normal weapon.
manual.sablelife.entity_hitbox.brief_tro: The box is normally invisible outside Preview. Check its active trigger and server box limit; another mod must deliver a supported damage event.
manual.sablelife.block_interaction.brief: Simulates an empty-hand right-click on the nearest supported block in a small area, on the structure or in the world.
Mark a reference face, select the interaction mode and aim the preview box at a door or button. Adjust start distance or offsets, then trigger once.
The preview box defines the interaction area. Only the nearest supported block is used; containers and crafting screens are skipped.
manual.sablelife.core.brief_usage: Core settings control the creature's health, regeneration, targeting, protection and death behavior. They apply to the whole creature; the Survival Heart Core has its own fixed rules and Energy costs.
manual.sablelife.module_management.brief: Add, rename, copy and organize abilities inside the core. Purple modules handle signals, red modules handle attacks, and yellow modules provide functions. Presets let you reuse a module's settings.
manual.sablelife.marking_system.brief_us: Marks choose a module's origin, direction or area. Most marks follow the marked part, while some modules use a fixed world point. A mark selects a location, not a player or mob.
manual.sablelife.preview_system.brief_us: Preview shows a module's origin, direction, area or movement path before use. Blueprint previews can also show block models. A preview helps check the setup, but does not guarantee that an action or placement can succeed.
manual.sablelife.triggers.brief_usage: Triggers decide when an enabled module runs. Use continuous activation, marked-point redstone or wireless signals, or let a Move set schedule several modules together.
manual.sablelife.wireless_channels.brief: Wireless Channel manages a core's local signals and external links. Internal channels connect modules within one core; matching red/blue frequency items link different cores or compatible devices. Wireless Redstone is a separate module.
manual.sablelife.survival_core.brief_usa: The Redstone Core controls supported modules on an assembled Sable structure without giving it health. Use it for signal-driven machines and automation; it is separate from the Energy-powered Survival Heart Core.
manual.sablelife.survival_heart_core.bri: The Survival Heart Core gives a Sable structure health and abilities in Survival mode. Refuel it with server-approved materials to pay for health, healing and paid modules. When life reaches zero, the structure releases automatically.
manual.sablelife.natural_spawning.brief_: The Wild Encounter Tool lets operators spawn server blueprints around players using rules for placement, density, faction and cleanup. Fixed-world crafting tables protect nearby areas. Release after spawning makes new objects independent of their rule.
manual.sablelife.server_limits.brief_usa: Server config controls module availability, resource limits and Survival Heart Core prices. These settings apply to the server and all connected players; client settings cannot override them.
manual.sablelife.move_set.brief_usage: Runs named moves made of timed module actions, allowing attacks, movement and effects to overlap. Conditions select eligible moves, then Priority or Weight chooses the next move. Ignore conditions allows behavior without a target.
manual.sablelife.health_phase.brief_usag: Outputs signals when the creature's health is within a chosen range or enters it. Use these signals to switch attacks, movement or effects between health phases.
manual.sablelife.damage_accumulation.bri: Tracks actual health lost and outputs a signal when accumulated damage reaches a threshold, or when damage during a timed window meets a chosen condition. It can also invert its output.
manual.sablelife.sequence.brief_usage: Plays a sequence of channel outputs and waiting periods. Use it to trigger several actions in order, either once or repeatedly while the input remains active.
manual.sablelife.wireless_redstone.brief: Outputs redstone at marked faces and can route signals to internal channels or external red/blue frequencies. It supports held signals, pulses and gradual changes in strength.
manual.sablelife.command.brief_usage: Runs virtual impulse, repeating and chain commands from the core. It requires command-block permissions and is intended for administrator-controlled behavior.
manual.sablelife.sensor.brief_usage: Detects eligible targets inside a chosen area and outputs a signal. It can drive attacks or automation through marked-face redstone, internal channels or external frequencies; only loaded targets can be detected.
manual.sablelife.navigation.brief_usage: Compares a target's direction with the structure's marked front and outputs directional redstone signals. Connect them to your movement or aiming mechanism; Target alignment itself does not move or turn the structure.
manual.sablelife.hit_counter.brief_usage: Counts successful health-damaging hits from a selected attack module and emits a pulse at the threshold. Use it to follow up an attack after a chosen number of hits.
manual.sablelife.signal_logic.brief_usag: Combines internal channel conditions using All or Any, then outputs a held signal or a rising-edge pulse. Use it to make an action depend on several signals.
manual.sablelife.combat_event.brief_usag: Emits pulses after attributed kills or blocked attacks. Own death can send an external pulse during an ordinary Heart Core's death process; a Survival Heart Core releases when life is depleted instead.
wild.sablelife.workbench_notice: Workbench protection: natural spawns avoid a %s-block horizontal radius around vanilla world crafting tables.
wild.sablelife.workbench_disabled: Workbench protection is disabled in server config.
wild.sablelife.workbench_notice_detail: Checks the full blueprint footprint, even in the air. Tables inside Sable structures are excluded. Radius: server config.
dashboard.sablelife.property_help.visual: Color of the pattern or symbol; presets and custom RGB are supported.
Base pattern radius; symbols use this value as text height.
Lifetime of one effect. Repeat mode emits additional effects.
Changes rotation, spark and plume speed independently of the lifetime.

Follow uses the part's current position and rotation. Fixed keeps the release pose. Contact effects stay at the contact point.
